Recommendation/Observation
33. The Committee is of the opinion that smart manufacturing is now making its place in the market
which is dependent on industrial automation including breath taking innovation viz. use of robots and
machine intelligence, smart material self learning systems etc. MSME sector requires integration of work
force and digital manufacturing and production processes for better performance. (Para 28)
Action taken
The Ministry of MSME is implementing the Technology Centre Systems Programme (TCSP) under
which 10 new Technology Centres are being set up apart from upgradation of the existing Technology

13
Centres. Smart manufacturing is now being introduced in a phased manner in the curricula of Technology
Centres. Some of the Technology Centres are already imparting training in Robotics, Internet of Things
(IoT), Industry 4.0. These Technology Centres are also using simulation software for training purpose.
Efforts are being made to provide exposure to latest technologies of Augmented Reality (AR) /Virtual Reality
(VR) /Artificial Intelligence (AI).
Recommendation/Observation
34. The Committee observes that implementation of some bigger scale IT project especially after the
introduction of GST and changes in tax structure involving business process across different Departments
which requires large amount of data entries requiring human resource during implementation. The SMEs are
often in shortage of manpower and thus it becomes difficult for them to carry out implementation as it is
always conflicting to run business on day to day basis with limited manpower and do the extra implementations
work. This affects the business enterprises in the nascent stage and forcing them to close the establishment
many a times. (Para 29)
Action Taken
Ministry of MSME is conducting various IT related programmes through their field offices mainly
Tool Rooms and MSME-DIs for the skill development to update the entrepreneurs about the latest technological
information. Ministry has also formulated a scheme for digital empowerment of MSMEs, which inter alia
aims at promotion of ICT applications such as by adoption of cloud computing in their production and
business processes.
Recommendation/Observation
35. The Committee is of the opinion that to fight with bankruptcy and insolvency, modern codes in this
area are need of the hour in the competitive markets and uncertainties in. globalization so that if an
entrepreneur is encouraged to take risk and the creditors should also have an assurance of disposal of case
quickly and repossession of assets after the failure of business. (Para 30)
Action Taken
The Ministry of Corporate Affairs has notified the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. The concern
of the Committee as expressed above has been shared with the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
Recommendation/Observation
36. The Committee observes that MSME sector having limited financial resources lags far behind in
adoption and acquisition of globally available expensive advanced technology and thus fails to stand
firmly in competitive and qualitative market. The Committee, therefore, recommends that a Global Technology
Acquisition Fund should be set up to enable the Indian Industries to acquire high-end technology with its
support to enhance their competitiveness globally and value addition. (Para 32)
Action Taken
The Ministry of MSME is also implementing the Technology Centre Systems Programme (TCSP)
under which 10 new Technology Centres are being set up apart from upgradation of the existing Technology
Centres. Smart manufacturing is now being introduced in a phased manner in the curricula of Technology
Centres.

14
Recommendation/Observation
37. The Committee recommends that R&D and Technology related support facilities and services including
training and skill development programme should cover optimum educated unemployed youths of the country
having qualification and talent along with inclination through IITs, ITIs, NITs and other research laboratories.
The facilities available need to be modernized and should be fine tuned and tailored as per the need and
requirement of the MSME sector. (Para 34)
Action Taken
The Ministry of MSME has involved national level premier institutes like Indian Institute of Technology
(IIT), Mumbai, Kanpur, Kharagpur, Roorkee and Guwahati, Indian Institute Sciences (lISc), Bangalore,
National Institute of Technology (NIT), Nagpur, Rourkela, Calicut and Silchar, Birla Institute of Technology
(BIT), Ranchi, College of Technology and Engineering (CTAE), Udaipur and North Eastern Regional lnstitute
of Science & Technology (NERIST), Itanagar as Technical Interfaces. Under these technical Interfaces,
various rural technologies suitable for KVI sector have been developed and also disseminated in the field.
Mahatma Gandhi Institute for Rural Industrialization (MGIRI), Wardha has been established to provide the
R & D and quality assurance input for the benefit of Khadi and V .I. Sector and to act as Hub & Spoke model
in between the technical interfaces. The Ministry of MSME is also implementing the scheme ASPIRE for
promoting incubation in rural sector. Till 31st March 2018, 62 LBIs have been approved and 30 commenced
incubation; over 18000 incubates have completed incubation; 30% have set up their own enterprises and
engaged in productive employment.
Further, in line with the recommendations of the Committee, modernization of the available facilities is
being encouraged as per the requirements of the MSME sector.
Recommendation/Observation
38. The Committee observes that the training in some cases is also imparted through NGOs who
take the training very casually and moreover, theoretical training is imparted as they lack practical
modules. (Para 51)
Action Taken
KVIC is organizing training programmes through 16 Departmental and 22 Non-Departmental Training
Centres. The NGO’s which are imparting training under the fold of KYIC are regularly being monitored by
State/Divisional Directors and their performance is being continuously reviewed. KYIC has introduced MIS
Package to monitor the performance of the training centres and the KYIC has also engaged the services of
Call Centre to get the feedback from the trainees regarding their experience in the training centre.
Recommendation/Observation
39. The recent innovative step to bring in fashion designer of repute to design Khadi fabrics is a welcome
move and it needs to be continued by bringing in more such steps. The Committee therefore recommends that
this along with good market techniques like frequent awareness campaigns among the youth and introduction
of Khadi in Schools. Hospitals and railways could be good recourse which will surely increase the demand
for Khadi products. Along with this, premier showrooms known as Khadi lounge should be opened in all the
States capitals and Airports to market designer Khadi products. (Para 53)

15
Action Taken
KVIC is promoting Khadi among the youth by participating in the events organized by Schools and
Colleges of repute. Moreover, during the exhibitions organized by KVIC, competitions like debate, essay
writing, cultural programmes, drawing competition, fashion show etc are also organized.
There are 26 items under Khadi, which have been registered in the Government e-Marketplace (GeM)
portal for supplies to Govt. Departments, PSUs, Railways etc. Railways are the largest consumer for Khadi
products with annual requirement of `60.00 crore approximately.
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Govt. of India has already issued directives to AIIMS,
NEIGRIHMS, JIPMER, PGI, NIMHANS, RIMS and others for procurement of 45 Khadi and Village Industry
items.
KVIC has opened Khadi Lounge at New Delhi, Mumbai, Jaipur and Bhopal. Exclusive sales outlets at
major airports have also been opened at Visakhapatnam, Ahmedabad and Lucknow. It is also proposed to
open 5 new sales outlets in major airports.
Recommendation/Observation
40. The Committee is of the view that the economic empowerment of the poor artisans can be enhanced by
more intervention by KVIC by allowing the spinners and weavers need to be allowed to work with the
private designers without the approval of KVIC so that they could earn more wages directly from these
designers. (Para 54)
Action Taken
The spinners/weavers are self-employed artisans of Khadi Institutions. There is no restriction by
KVIC on any Khadi Institution and artisans to associate themselves with private designers. Under the KVIC-
Raymond agreement many Khadi Institutions have been encouraged to supply directly, to enable the artisans
to get better wages.
Recommendation/Observation
41. The Committee observes that the urban youths are not inclined to work in this sector due to low wages
and the hardships involved in it. The Committee recommends that the issue of low wages of unskilled, semi
skilled artisans needs to be addressed on priority as the availability of more willing workers will bring in more
quality outcome in Khadi sector . This would help in increasing the benefits to the artisans. (Para 55)
Action Taken
Recently, Ministry of MSME approved a proposal of KYIC to enhance the wages of spinners from
` 5.50 to ` 7.50 per hand to attract more youth to Khadi sector. With the initiatives taken by- KVIC, to
associate the private sector players and setting up of franchisees, it is expected that the youth will be more
attracted to this sector.
Recommendation/Observation
42. The Committee is of the opinion that the minimum educational qualification prescribed under the
PMEGP and absence of the option of regional language in publicity/procedural formality may be the probable
reasons hampering the proper implementation of the flagship scheme as a potential entrepreneur with low

16
education profile may be prone to face difficulties in completion of all procedural formalities including
filling up of form. In this regard, necessary steps should be taken to address the problem. (Para 66)
Action Taken
As regards publicity, the advertisements are published allover the country in regional languages also.
For the filing the online application and procedural formality, the option of English and Hindi language is
available on the e-portal of flagship scheme of Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme
(PMEGP).
To solve the difficulties of potential entrepreneurs in completion of all the procedural formalities
including filling up of form due to low education profile, RUDSETI/RSETI offer handholding services to the
trainees for a period of 2 years to address teething problems if any and to facilitate the sanction of loan and
to ensure that the units are properly grounded.
Recommendation/Observation
43. The Committee also observes that only half the targeted projects set up by KVIC have been approved/
disbursed by the Banks which does not portray a rosy scenario. The Committee desires that the Ministry
may step in to r esolve the problems in consultation with KVIC and financial institutions so that targets set
forth are achieved. (Para 67)
Action Taken
KVlC invites online application under PMEGP scheme. The applications received are placed before the
District Level Task Force Committee (DLTFC). Further, DLTFC takes interview of the candidates and
assess the capability according to type of project to be set up by the entrepreneur. The projects of candidates
recommended by DLTFC are forwarded to the financing banks as per the choice of candidate. The financing
banks assess the techno-economic viability of the projects and sanction the funds according to banking
norms after assessment of the credit profile of the borrowers.
The KVIC and the Ministry hold meetings with the Banks and Nodal officers of Banks on a regular
basis to ensure that the targets are achieved.
Recommendation/Observation
44. The Committee is of the opinion that MSMEs are an integral part of the economic development of the
country and therefore their growth and survival is vital for the Government. Hence, it recommends that more
and more MSME exposition, MSME Haats and MSME National/International trade fairs/Exhibitions should
be organized, including at District level, with the participation of people’s representatives, to enhance the
market accessibility of MSMEs. (Para 91)
Action Taken
Various steps are taken by the Ministry [or MSME to give a better exposure to MSMEs in domestic
and international market for their products/ services. Under the existing Marketing Assistance Scheme and
Special Marketing Assistance Scheme of NSSH, National Small Industries Corporation Ltd. (NSIC) a PSU
under this Mini stry acts as a facilitator to promote marketing efforts and enhance the competency of the
micro, small and medium enterprises for capturing the new market opportunities by way of organizing!
participating in various domestic and international exhibitions/trade fairs, buyer-seller meets, intensive-

17
campaigns and other marketing events. NSIC helps micro and small enterprises to participate in International/
National exhibitions/trade fairs at the subsidized rates to exhibit and market their products. Participation in
the marketing events provides micro, small and medium enterprises an exposure to the National/International
markets.
Further, under International Cooperation Scheme, financial assistance is provided on reimbursement
basis to the State/Central Government organizations, industries/enterprises Associations and registered
societies/trusts and organizations associated with MSME for deputation of MSME business delegation to
other countries for exploring new areas of MSMEs, participation by Indian MSMEs in international exhibitions,
trade fairs, buyer seller meet and for holding international conference and seminars which are in the interest
of MSME sectors.
Recommendation/Observation
45. Deforestation is one of the major threats for the maintenance of ecological balance. The Committee,
in order to avoid grave threats which are endangering the climatic conditions and human life, recommends
that the production of substitutes for wood, such as coir wood, has to be encouraged and more coir
clusters under SFURTI have to be established to meet the demands of coir based furnishings and building
materials from the domestic as well as international market. To achieve this, more funds should be
allocated by the Ministry of MS&ME to the Coir Board with proper monitoring and utilization of allocated
funds. (Para 106)
Action Taken
Against the BE 2017-18 of  `75 crore, an allocation of `125 crore has been earmarked under SUFRTI..
Automatically, the share of Coir Board will be higher than the previous year. Under the Scheme of Fund for
Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI), the Government of India has sanctioned financial assistance
for establishment of two clusters for production of Needled Felt coir composite panels. Further, Coir Board
has proposed establishment of another cluster in Tamil Nadu viz. Salem, for production of needled felt based
coir composite panels. In addition to this, Coir Board is taking all out efforts to take up new cluster proposals
under SFURTI 2nd Phase exclusively for manufacturing coir wood and related products.
Recommendation/Observation
46. The Committee is of the firm opinion that in order to have a better co-ordination of export promotion
of coir and its by products for aiding in multifarious activities such as soil erosion control, landscaping,
river embankment etc., establishment of overseas offices of the Coir Board may be considered. This way, the
Coir Industry would also grow internationally side by side with the Khadi Industry. (Para 107)
Action Taken
Coir Board is regularly participating in the Annual Conference and Expo of International Erosion
Control Association in America which is a global platform for addressing erosion control issues. Application
of coir geo-textiles in erosion control, landscaping and rural road construction have immense potential
world over because of the eco-friendly nature when compared to synthetic products and other natural
fibers. In order to popularize the use of coir gee-textiles abroad, Coir Board has plans for organizing field
demonstrations on the application of coir gee-textiles and such other initiatives for capturing potential markets
abroad. The proposal for establishing overseas offices has already been included in the future action plans of
the Board. For meeting the expenditure involved the possibilities of convergence with the Market Access

18
Initiative (MAI) scheme of the Ministry of Commerce and the support of the Ministry of External affairs will
be explored.
Recommendation/Observation
47. The Coir Board is implementing multifarious developmental and promotional activities when in
turn is providing employment to a large number of people mostly in the rural areas of the country.
Sufficient manpower is however required for implementation and monitoring the programmes and for
providing research data/statistics in time for MIS. Hence, the Committee recommends that in view of the
increased activities of the Board. the necessary qualified manpower should be provided to the Board for
its smooth functioning. (Para 108)
Action Taken
It is to mention that a High Level Official Committee was constituted for reviewing and assessment of
the direct recruitment vacancies existing in Coir Board, creation of new posts, posts to be provided as
matching savings towards creation/upgradation of posts etc. The Committee, after assessment of the relevant
factors, recommended to impress upon the Ministry the essentiality for immediate filling up of the direct
recruitment vacancies, which include a number of technical posts to be positioned in Field Offices like
Regional Offices/ Sub Regional Offices, through which Plan programmes are implemented and accord
sanction for the same. Similarly, it has also been recommended to follow up the proposal for creation of 20
senior level new posts, already under the consideration of the Ministry, which are also equally important
against the necessity for more effective implementation of the schemes in coir sector with increased budgetary
support.
Recommendation/Observation
48. The Committee is aware that there are various other schemes implemented by the Government under
which technology developed is transferred to the beneficiaries without any charges. The Committee is therefore
is of the view that the technology developed by the Coir Board should be transferred to entrepreneurs,
traders, clusters etc. free of cost to encourage potential entrepreneurs to get into the coir sector. Besides,
steps should also be taken to explore the potential overseas markets for export of coir products particularly
innovative coir products. Also, 100% modernization of coir industry has to be encouraged with high funding
support to popularize the innovative coir products in domestic market as well. (Para 115)
Action Taken
The Government of India has from time to time emphasized the need of its organizations becoming
self-supporting through income generation activities. Earnings through transfer of technology are a source
of income for Coil’ Board. However, free transfer of technology can be considered on a case to case basis
depending on the category of beneficiaries, area of improvement, etc. For instance, technologies that could
improve the productivity of workers, quality of products, etc. could be transferred free of cost. In order to
expand the overseas markets for Indian coir products, the Coir Board is implementing programmes like
participation in international exhibitions and buyer seller meets. Under this programme, the Board undertake
the following activities:
(i) Organise national participation in international fairs abroad.
(ii) Organise participation in international fairs in India.

19
(iii) Organise exclusive international fairs for coir in India and abroad.
(iv) Or ganise Buyer Seller Meets abroad for coir.
(v) Organise reverse Buyer Seller Meets in India.
(vi) Or ganise participation in Seminars, Conferences, Workshops etc. abroad.
(vii) Organise display of coir products in the premises of Indian Missions.
(viii) Undertake demonstrations projects on a pilot scale, conducting seminars etc based on a focus
product/ focus market approach with a view to educate and establish the end use applications of
specific products like coir gee-textiles, coir wood etc. among the target audience.
In addition to the above, the Board is implementing the External Market Development Assistance
scheme with the objective of encouraging the small scale exporters to enter global market and to expand the
export of Indian coir products. Under this scheme, the eligible entrepreneurs will get reimbursement of
space rent, air fare, freight charges, etc. for participation in international exhibitions/buyer seller meets as
per the eligibility conditions and scale of assistance prescribed in the scheme.
Recommendation/Observation
49. The Committee is also of the opinion that Buyer Seller meets and Vendor Development Programmes
may be organized overseas to popularize coir products and to tap the virgin overseas markets. (Para 116)
Action Taken
Ministry of MSME is already organising International Trade Fair to popularize the various product
including coir product and to see the opportunity for marketing of their products.
Recommendation/Observation
50. The Committee was informed about the Solar Charkha Mission for which an allocation of 
` 50 crores
has been made for the first time during 2018-19. Though the Solar Charkha mode will surely remove
drudgery, the Committee is of the view that the KVlC should ensure that there is no conflict in the definition
of Khadi which originally was totally ‘hand spun’, but with the introduction of Solar Charkha, it would
become ‘motorized’. (Para 121)

Solar cloth produced out of solar yarn from Solar Charkha has been categorized under Village Industries
activities by the Ministry vide Ministry’s letter bearing No.A54/ 711/2015-KVlC-P dated 14.01.2016 and
subsequent Commission’s Circular No. RID/New Development of Solar Charkha/2015-16 dated 06/
08.02.2016.
Ministry of MSME has made an allocation of `50.00 crore for the Solar Charkha Mission for the year
2018-19, as detailed below:
Grant-in-Aid General : ` 13.00 crores
SCC : ` 18.00 crores
STC : ` 09.00 crores

20
NER : ` 10.00 crores
TOTAL : ` 50.00 crores
Hence, there is no conflict in the definition of Khadi (Hand spun and Hand woven), as Solar Vastra
(Solar power spun and woven) has been categorized under Village Industry.
Recommendation/Observation
51. The Committee is of the view that the Ministry of MS&ME should consider other available options to
provide necessary raw materials required by the MSMEs and for this, the other concerned Ministries/
Departments be persuaded for allocation of raw materials like, aluminum, copper, paraffin wax, cement
and bitumen etc. to fulfill the requirement of MSME sector. (Para 140)
Action Taken
In order to provide necessary raw materials required by the MSMEs certain quantities of raw materials
should be allocated by the main producers under Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) with special
discount for distribution to MSMEs through NSIC. Materials like Polymer Products, Bitumen, Copper,
Zinc, Paraffin Wax and Pig Iron should be provided so that MSMEs can be benefitted.
Recommendation/Observation
52. The Committee is of the considered opinion that the Incubation Centres run by NSIC provide training
to the prospective entrepreneurs by imparting training in the manufacturing as well as service sector for skill
development. In view of the huge skill demand existing in the country, the Committee recommends that more
Incubation Centres should be established in co-ordination with State Government so that training in
conventional trade as well as hi-tech areas are imparted to entrepreneurs to accure skill in all areas of
business operation for gainful employment. (Para 141)
Action Taken
In order to expand the setting up of Incubation Centres, ‘A Scheme for Promoting Innovation, Rural
Industry and Entrepreneurship (ASPIRE)’ is being implemented to promote Innovation and Rural
Entrepreneurship through rural Livelihood Business Incubator (LEI), Technology Business Incubator (TEI)
and Fund of Funds for start-up creation. The awareness of ASPIRE Scheme is being created among State
Governments as well as academic institutions. Also, under TCSP, 15 new Technology Centres are being
established in 14 States of the country including North-Eastern State. All these new Technology Centres
have provision for setting up of Manufacturing Incubation Centre (MIC) to develop (incubate) innovative
ideas of MSMEs/new entrepreneurs. Manufacturing Incubation Centre in 10 Technology Centres are scheduled
to commence in by June, 2019.
Recommendation/Observation
53. The Committee observes that as per reply furnished by the Ministry under the Single Point Registration
Scheme (SPRS), there are 527 MSMEs registered upto 15
th February, 2018. However , as per the Annual
Report, 2017-18, there were 21922 cumulative numbers of units registered under SPRS upto 31st December,
2017. The Committee desires that mismatch between the figures should be clarified and placed before the
Committee. (Para 143)

21
Action Taken
A total number of 21515 units (upto 31.03.2018) were registered under Single Point Registration
Scheme of NSIC including units belonging to SC/ST category registered with 100% fee subsidy under
National SC/ST Hub with 100% fee subsidy.
Under National SC/ST Hub, 100% subsidy on fee of NSIC for fresh registration/renewal of registration

under SPRS was the MSMEs registered with special subsidy under SPRS of National SC/ST Hub.

54. The Committee feels that use of standard raw material consistently; possible design development,
process and product development including planning for maximum output, maximum efficiency, better
finishing with accuracy can sharpen the competitiveness in manufacturing and production sector. MSMEs
face competition from developing countries due to globalization and increased international trade but most
of the Micro and Small Enterprises do not see financial competition as major deterring factor but tend to
face stiff competition in quality rather than prices. (Para 152)
Action Taken
The new Technology Centres being established under the TCSP will be equipped with latest technology/
manufacturing processes, which will assist MSMEs in the development of quality product and enhance their
competitiveness. Further, the various components of the NMCP scheme would assist in enhancing the
competitiveness of the MSMEs in the relevant sector.
Recommendation/Observation
55. To enhance the marketing, targeted advertising through social network sites may prove a right
platform to reach out to prospective customers. The Committee feels that Ministry of MS&ME should
emphasize on setting up of more LBIs and TBIs with modern practice and procedure for skill up-gradation
of MSMEs. (Para 153)
Action Taken
Under ‘A Scheme for Promotion of Innovation, Rural Industry and Entrepreneurship (ASPIRE)” 62
LBIs and 8 TBIs were approved till 31
st March 2018. In the current version, the Scheme Steering Committee
has considered 13 proposals. During the current year and next year, more LBIs would be set up for skill up-
gradation and creation of more employment opportunities.
Recommendation/Observation
56. The Committee observes that benefits under CLCSS are extended to the beneficiaries only through 11
Banks. The Committee recommends that more Banks should be added to the list of banks. Moreover, the list
of 51 subsectors should be increased in consultation with Industry Associations and GTAB. The Ministry of
MS&ME should also ensure release of timely payment to scheduled Banks. (Para 165)
Action Taken
Under the Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (CLCSS), II Nodal banks/Financial institutions have
been identified as the nodal banks/agencies who implement the scheme in collaboration with the co-opted

22
Scheduled Commercial Banks, Scheduled Cooperative Banks [including the urban cooperative banks co-
opted by the SIDBI under the Technological Up-gradation Fund Scheme (TUFs) of the Ministry of Textiles],
Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), State Financial Corporations (SFCs), the North Eastern Development Financial
Institution (NEDFI) who are eligible as Prime Lending Institutions (PLIs) under this scheme only after they
execute a General Agreement (GA) with any of the nodal agencies, i.e. the Small Industries Development
Bank of India (SIDBI) and National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD).
In regard to the list of 51 sub-sectors, it is to submit that the proposal of the continuation of the CLCS
Scheme is underway, wherein it has been specified that the list of the sectors will be updated dynamically.
Further, it is also submitted that the proposal of the inclusion of some more new sector/sub-sector was
placed before the 7th GTAB held on 27.09.2016, but the proposal could not be approved due to inadequate
availability of funds.

CHAPTER-III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS  IN  RESPECT  OF  WHICH  THE  COMMITTEE
HAS  NOT  ACCEPTED  THE  REPLIES  OF  THE  MINISTRY  AND  DESIRE  THE  MINISTRY
TO  REVIEW  THEIR  REPLIES
Recommendation/Observation
57. The Ministry of MSME submitted during the examination of Demands 2018-19, that the budget under
certain Schemes could not be utilized properly as the schemes are demand driven. The Committee therefore
suggests that proper assessment regarding financial requirement of the demand driven Schemes should be
made by the Ministry before sending the Budget proposals. Hence, it should be ensured in future that the
budget allocation made is utilized properly and overrated demands are not projected by any of the organization/
Institution under its jurisdiction. (Para 17)
Action Taken
The suggestion of the Committee has been noted. The Ministry of MSME has taken following measures
in order to enhance the demand of its schemes:
 Organising of Udyam Samwad (dialogue with various associations and enterprises), Interaction
with Heads/Representatives of field institutes and regular meetings with Industry Associations
& Chamber of Commerce.
 Visits by Nodal Officers and their representatives to the selected 115 Aspirational Districts across
the country to assess the needs of the area in terms of skilling, employment generation and
enterprise development. The nodal officers hold interactions with different stakeholders to get
suggestions for better implementation of schemes of the .Ministry.
Launch of various Portals like Udyog Aadhar Memorandum (UAM) on 19.09.2015, MSME SAMADHAN
(to address delayed payment to MSEs) on 30.09.2017, MSME SAMBANDH (for Public Procurement
from MSEs) on 08.12.207 and UDYAM SAMPARK to facilitate development of various aspects of
enterprises.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee may be informed about the impact of various measures such as launching of
varoius e-portals, visits to 115 Aspirational districts, organising Udyog Samwad etc. taken by the M/
o MSME to monitor the financial requirements of the demand driven schemes. Further, the
Committee may be informed whether there has been better utilisation of funds as a result of the
said measures under-taken by the Ministry.
Recommendation/Observation
58. The Committee feels that there is an urgent need to evaluate the Research and Development system
to make it more effective and beneficial to the MSME sector which is crawling far behind in technology
adoption in comparison to MSMEs of developed countries. The Committee recommends that Ministry of
MS&ME being the protector of the units in this sector should allocate more funds for R&D and
qualified people working in the field be motivated and encouraged through the best possible ways and
means. (Para 35)
23

24
Action Taken
Evaluation of the Research and Development projects has been periodically undertaken by KVIC
through various reputed agencies. Collaborative action with CSIR laboratories is also being taken for the
promoting MSME centric research and technology transfer.
Further Recommendation/Observation
In view of fast and new technological innovations and advancements taking place across the
world in MSME and related sectors, the Committee recommends that a dedicated fund should be set
up for the Research & Development purposes only for adoption of improved technology and
innovations in the field of MSME to keep the pace with the MSMEs of the developing and developed
countries. Further, evaluation of the R&D projects should be undertaken on a regular and time
bound basis by reputed agencies under the strict monitoring of the M/o MSME through a team
having a nodal officer for the purpose.
Recommendation/Observation
59. The Committee notes that the constraint faced by KVIC/KVIB is mainly due to procedural delays,
inadequate technology up-gradation, improper utilization of funds etc. Despite providing technical guidance
to the units in KVI, the problems of the units remain inadequately addressed. This is one of the reason for sub
optimal functioning of institutions/units and high drop outs among new entrants, low employment generation.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that KVIC in view of the expansion of its area of operation in every
nook and corner of the Country, should come forward with a more holistic and unified policy in co-ordination
with the Ministry of MS&MEs and other stakeholders as regards the successful operation of the units is
concerned. Proper planning, monitoring and implementation in each scheme is required to meet the primary
objective of employment generation along with proper utilization of the budgetary support in view of year
on year enhancement in it. (Para 49)
Action Taken
The KVIC implements various programmes with a view to generating sustainable employment under
the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP). 48398 projects have been set up and
employment opportunities have been provided to 3.87 lakh persons with Margin Money subsidy amounting
` 1312.40 crore during the year 2017-18.
The BE for 2018-19 has been fixed at `1800.64 crore to facilitation larger coverage under the flagship
scheme.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee reiterates its suggestion that the KVIC, in co-ordination with the Ministry
and other stakeholders, should come up with an effective mechanism for proper planning, monitoring
and implementation of each scheme under it.
Recommendation/Observation
60. The C ommittee feels that in face of stiff competition in the market from Organized industries
KV1s should concentrate more on its technology improvement and products upgradation. It therefore
recommends that regular training by efficient staff having experience and expertise should be imparted

25
to the ar tisans through its network of training institutions. A r egular study on the functioning of the
training institutions sh ould be conducted as the present methods and practices may be outdated and not be
that much effective. The Committee recommends that the process of revamping and reorientation of KV1s
should also- be done wherever required so that it helps in productivity and development of Khadi and
Village Industries. (Para 50)
Action Taken
Under the Khadi Reform and Development Programme, selected Khadi Institutions have been given
funds tor up-gradation of infrastructure, sales outlets and capacity building of artisans. This has led to
increase in production and turnover of KVI sector in the last two years.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee recommends that modern practices and technology prevailing in the global
markets should be studied and adopted for KVIs and manpower employed in the KVIs should be
equipped with necessary skills and training for better performance of the KVIs in every aspect.
Lack of raw material and equipment should not hinder their performance in any way. The wages of
the artisans should also be adequate enough so that they can live satisfactorily, respectfully and
contribute their 100% for betterment of KVIs because a satisfied employee contributes immensely
for an establishment. Modern marketing practices and strategies should also be adopted in the
wake of cut-throat competition in the market.
Recommendation/Observation
61. The Committee observes that KVIC is not working impressively in North Eastern Region and has a
very small set up in these areas. The number of ISEC issued under Khadi and Polyvastra is almost negligible
except in Assam and Manipur in the last financial year. The Committee desires that the reasons for the same
other than the hardships faced due to hilly terrain should be placed before it. (Para 76)
Action Taken
KVIC has extended necessary support to KIs of NER region. KVIC is also encouraging Khadi and V .I.
institutions to implement Khadi Reform and Development Programme (KRDP) and Honey Mission
programmes.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee desires that the root cause of the poor performance of the KIs in NER should
be ascertained by the Ministry of MSME and appropriate remedial steps be taken to address the
problem as it will help in addressing the problem of unemployment and insurgency in NER. A
special roadmap keeping in view the geographical features/difficulties of the NER should be prepared
by the Ministry for improving the performance of KVIC in NER as already apprised to the Committee.
The Ministry should also find out the shortcomings in the implementation of its policies specifically
in NER.
Recommendation/Observation
62. The Com mittee is of the Opinion that KYIC which is mandated for providing employment
opportun ities across the country must come out with a comprehensive plan considering the local need for

26
the Khadi as well as for village industries sector along with developing a marketing network for rural
Khadi artisans. (Para 86)
Action Taken
The KVIC is enhancing its footprint across the country. The funding of khadi and village industries
projects is also being taken up under PMEGP across the country. It is proposing a comprehensive scheme
for providing employment opportunities in 117 aspirational districts.
Further Recommendation/Observation
New marketing strategies and policies should be devised by the Ministry in consultation with
KVIC and KVIB for Khadi artisans keeping in view the rural set up of the country. The Committee
would like to know about the details of the comprehensive scheme for providing employment in 117
Aspirational Districts mentioned by Ministry.
Recommendation/Observation
63. The Committee observes that first and foremost requirement is overhauling of the marketing strategy
for KVI products. Product development and marketing need a professional approach. Even the attempts
to boost sales using Khadi as brand name is unlikely 10 succeed unless some fundamental changes arc
introduced. Bringing in, the private sector for marketing and product development may be a good attempt
and may be initiated as a pilot project. KVIC and M/o MS&ME should think over the cost cutting and
stoppage of rebate on sale. The Committee desires that an enhanced B.E. of 
` 65 crores under MPDA for
2018-19 may be utilized judiciously for organizing Trade Fairs, Vendor Development Programmes etc. at
domestic and international levels so that a need to bring down the funds drastically at the RE stage does
not arise. (Para 90)
Action Taken
KVIC is engaging professional agencies to develop strategies for boosting marketing and product
development the new Marketing trends and avenues for KVI products. For promotion of Khadi products
exclusively by the private partners, KVIC has entered into agreement with M/s Raymonds, M/s Aditya Birla
Group and M/s Arvind Textiles.
For better marketing of KVI products KVIC has also entered into agreement for shop-in-shop model
“Khadi Korner” with M/s Globus Stores and Mis Apna Bazaar. Discussions are underway with M/s Big
Bazaar and Indian Merchant Chambers. During the year 2018-19, KVIC proposes to open 15 new “Khadi
Korner” stores.
Apart from this, KVIC has opened 6 exclusive KVI products franchisees at Pune, Mumbai,
Thiruvananthapuram and New Delhi. During the year 2018-19 KVIC proposes to organize and participate in
number of exhibitions in the domestic market. Participation in International Exhibitions is also encouraged.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee is of the opinion that to increase profitability of the KVI products, the current
marketing trends and practices should be adopted. Internet can be a very good platform for
marketing and promotion of KVI products. The Ministry is advised to make full use of the internet
as a marketing platform for increasing saleability of KVI products. Further, tentative schedule of

27
Domestic/International exhibitions should be included in the Annual Report of the Ministry of
MS&ME in order to increase the number of participants in such exhibitions for popularizing KVI
products.
Recommendation/Observation
64. The Committee feels that one of the most important objectives of the implementation of various
Schemes under Coir Board is the employment generation especially in rural areas. For this, an organization
like Coir Board is providing training on various aspects of production and development of new/innovative
products. The Committee recommends that Ministry of MS&ME should give a consideration for recognition
of such training courses/training institutions so that younger generation will be attracted to such training
and the status of such training will be elevated to the next level. (Para 100)
Action Taken
As recommended by the Committee, giving recognition to training courses offered by Coir Board and
other training institutions by the Govt. of India will authenticate the value of the course and encourage
potential employers to hire the successful trainees.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee recommends that effective training programmes/courses be introduced by
professionals/experts to provide quality training for various schemes under Coir Board to attract
prospective trainees from younger generation, which will create more job opportunities in rural
areas. In this regard, the Ministry of MSME should take up the issue of authentication of courses,
in consultation with Coir Board, with the.Government. Adequate steps should also be taken to
improve the working conditions and wages in Coir Industry so that more people become part of it.
Recommendation/Observation
65. The Committee also desires that the Ministry in consultation with the Coir Board should make all out
efforts to reach out to the Coir Udyami Yojna applicants whose accounts arc frequently turning to NP As
resulting in Banks shuwing reluctance to sanction loans under the Scheme. The Ministry of MSME should
make efforts to ascertain the root cause of increasing rate of NP As under the Scheme. (Para 101)
Action Taken
Coir Board had initiated several steps to address the issue of NPA under the erstwhile Scheme of Coir
Udyami Yojana. The Board, in association with the Banks, conducted awareness/sensitization programmes
for the applicants on the need of prompt repayment of the loan and successful functioning of the unit
established under the Scheme. Besides, Adalats/recovery camps were organized in association with the
Banks for the defaulters and the Banks have been able to recover the dues to some extent. Having regard to
these difficulties, the Scheme was modified by including provisions for working capital and marketing
support assistance. The scheme has been merged with the PMEGP for better provisions/reach and will be
implemented from the financial year, 2018-19.
Further Recommendation/Observation
Apart from organizing Adalats/recovery camps, the Ministry is advised to find out the root
cause of rising cases of NPAs and take remedial steps immediately as it adversely affects the whole

28
scheme. The Committee would also like to know about the considerations, which have influenced
the merger of the scheme with PMEGP and likely positive outcome thereof as the Scheme was
modified earlier also.
Recommendation/Observation
66. A maximum numbers of coir industries are in Micro and Small category and these are dependant
heavily on the Banks and other financial institutions for funds. Natural calamities like. tsunami/cyclones
etc. which are beyond the control of human being, sometimes badly effects the coir industries destroying
them seriously. The Committee therefore, recommends that in such cases, the coir sector should be supported
financially in order to provide some relief to the affected artisans/ units and, for the purpose, a corpus fund
specifically, for Coir Board may be a good solution and could be considered positively. (Para 117)
Action Taken
The recommendation of the DRPSC to provide relief to coir industrial units when destruction is
caused by natural calamities would go a long way in stabilizing the coir industry. The industry is more or less
spread across the coastal belt of the country where natural calamities affect most. There have been many
instances of wiping out of coir industry due to cyclones in the past. If funds are allocated to meet such
exigencies in the annual budget of Coir Board, the needy stakeholders can be assisted promptly and the
industry can be saved from setbacks. If unutilized, the Corpus fund allocated for the purpose can be carried
forward to the next year.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee is of the view that necessary steps may be taken up with Ministry of Finance
for- allocation of funds in the annual budget of the Coir Board to meet such exigency for assistance
of stakeholders.
Recommendation/Observation
67. The Committee observes that NSIC through its Vendor Development Programme sensitize and facilitate
MSEs, including SC/ST MSEs, to become qualified vendors to public sector units and other Government
Departments as per the provision of 20% mandatory procurement under Public Procurement Policy. Of this,
4% should be from SC/ST MSEs. While the PSUs and Government procurement from MSEs has been gradually
improving, procurement from SC/ST units is still very low. Therefore, the Committee recommends that there
should be more VDPs organised to publicise Public Procurement Policy among MSEs including SC/ST
units. (Para 142)
Action taken
In order to improve the procurement of CPSEs from SC/ST MSEs the Corporation organized 60 nos.
of Special YDPs for SC/ST entrepreneurs across the country during FY . 2017- 18. A total of 1889 SC/ST
entrepreneurs participated in these SYDPs. In addition to the above, 22 State Conclaves were organized
under National SC/ST Hub during F.Y . 2017-18 with the-objective to create awareness on Public Procurement
Policy 2012 (PPP-2012) and provide common platform for SC/ST entrepreneurs, CPSEs, Industry
Associations and Bankers for enhancing participation of SC/ST MSEs in Public Procurements.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee is of the opinion that procurement from SC/ST MSEs is not very impressive

29
and encouraging despite organising Vendor Development Programmes and taking various other
measures by the Ministry to .sensitize the SC/ST entrepreneurs. The Committee recommends
that the Ministry may pay special attention to this issue and take measures to increase the
participation of SC/ST entrepreneurs under the Public Procurement Policy and apprise the Committee
accordingly.
Recommendation/Observation
68. The Committee is pleased to note that the launch of the UAM has proved to be a stepping stone for the
ease of doing Business by the MSMEs. However, at the same time it also observes that the online filling
system under UAM based on self declared information shows an uneven geographical distribution of UAMs
across all Indian States and Union Territories. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Ministry
should take the required steps to encourage MSMEs, especially, the Small and Medium Enterprises to
register under UAM. In this direction, the stakeholders from the States/UT Governments, Industry Associations
and Public at large should also be encouraged to contribute significantly for the purpose, especially in the
NER, in order to afford ease of doing business in the MSME sector. (Para 148)
Action Taken
State conclaves are being organized in various parts of the country under National SC/ST Hub scheme.
Through these conclaves this Ministry is creating awareness of various endeavors undertaken by the Central
Government including Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum (UAM). The Ministry is coordinating with States/UTs/
industry associations to increase awareness about UAM and facilitate registration under UAM. These State
Level Conclaves also provide helpdesk for enrolment of UAM.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee recommends that Ministry should pay special attention to get maximum Udyog
Aadhar Memorandum (UAM) registrations from NER as the registraions in NER are still very low
and there is clearly a geographical imbalance in UAM registrations. The Ministry should organise
special camps/prog rammes with the support of local bodies and Industry Associations to create
awareness among the entrepreneurs of NER and create a conducive environ m cut for
entrepreneurship in NER.
Recommendation/Observation
69. The Committee finds that there is a tangible gap in subsidy claims received and settled every year.
There is also a declining trend in the number of MSEs benefitted. The Committee is constrained to note the
decreasing trend in subsidy claim amount. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of MS&ME should
come out with a concrete plan to get sufficient allocation from the Ministry of Finance for clearance of
subsidy claims. (Para 164)
Action Taken
The tangible gap in subsidy claims received and settled every year and decreasing trend in subsidy
claim amount is due to lack of allocation of the funds in the appropriate head. This Ministry has taken up the
matter of additional fund allocation at various levels with M/o Finance to liquidate the pendency of ` 985.00
Crore. The Committee may like to also direct M/o Finance in this regard.

30
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee expresses its grave concern over the pending claims of MSME under CLCSS
to the tune of ````` 985 crores. The Committee recommends M/o MSME should convey the feelings of
the Committee to the M/o Finance and request them to provide budget allocation for full settlement
of pending claims. The Committee may be informed of the response of the M/o Finance by the first
week of January, 2019.
Recommendation/Observation
70. The Committee expresses its reservation over low employability under PMEGP during 2017-18
and feels that without raising the employability, the Scheme would be wastage of resources. The
Committee expects the Ministry to inform it about the concrete steps taken to improve employability
in NER. (Para 172)
Action Taken
 Targets under PMEGP are set in terms of Margin Money (MM) allocation. Projects are indicative.
 During the year 2017 -18, the employment rate was estimated eight persons per project under PMEGP.
While fixing the targets average MM per project was taken as `2.00 lakh, however, in actual the MM
per project comes to `2.70 lakh due to increase in project size which results in less number of projects
set up during 2017-18 and proportionately less projects.
 The fixation of targets in terms of number of projects will be set up taking average margin money at-
least ` 2.5 lakh per project during 2018-19.
 As per the scheme guidelines the employment is expected to be generated as per the capital expenditure
(plant/machinery/building) and working capital varies from project to project.
 The quantum of beneficiary’s contribution and rate of subsidy (MM) admissible to the NE region
under the PMEGP scheme is as under:
Category Beneficiary’s Rate of Subsidy
Contribution (percentage )
(on project cost) Urban Rural
All categories in N.E Region 5% 25% 35%
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Ministry has furnished only data and has not apprised the Committee about the steps,
which would be taken to increase employability in NER. The Committee desires the details of the
steps to be taken or have already been taken by the Ministry for increasing the employability in
NER.

CHAPTER-IV
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE COMMITTEE DESIRE
FURTHER COMMENTS OF THE MINISTRY
Recommendation/Observation
71. The Committee notes that the MGIRI is the only Institution under the Ministry of MSME which is
working on empowerment of traditional artisans through R&D projects for alternative technology using
local resources and it has given excellent results, especially, with regard to the project based on cow urine
and waste human hair producing Amino acid as a plant growth promoter. The Committee observes that the
success of this pilot project would go a long way in increasing employment generation in the rural areas of
the Country. The Committee is of the view that there should not be any shortage of funds for the institution
rather it should be promoted and motivated. (Para 126)
Action Taken
Mahatma Gandhi Institute for Rural Industrialization (MGIRI) has put a lot of efforts to develop
various innovative technologies/products in the area of Khadi & Textile, Food-processing, herbal, Panchgavya,
agri-inputs, chemical based industries, rural craft & engineering, rural energy & infrastructure. Few
remarkable technologies such as Amino acid mixture, Panchgavya based various products, Flavored Soya
milk & Calcium rich tofu, Potter’s wheel, Blunger, Solar Charkha, Ponduru tool, Soft and stiff finish
technology etc. have been commercially disseminated successfully and there is marked improvement in the
number of rural enterprises, benefitted through skill development/ entrepreneurship development programmes
conducted in last few years. MGIRI has also got success in filling 26 patents on various technologies/
products and in publication of research papers in reputed national and international journals. MGIRI is also
working in collaboration with KYIC in the field of S&T, SFURTI cluster development and KRDP programmes
etc..
MGIRI can support in Prime Minister’s flagship programmes such as “Make In India”, “Start Up
India” etc. and KVIC’s schemes like PMEGP, SFURTI etc. more effectively by way of widen rich of
MGIRI as focus institute for rural industrialization, entrepreneurial development, facilitating marketing,
testing and financial support to prospective entrepreneurs.

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry, having
been authorised by the Committee, hereby present this Two Hundred Ninety Fourth Report on Micro,
Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2018 pertaining to the Ministry of Micro,
Small and Medium Enterprises.
2. In pursuance of Rule 270 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Council of
States relating to the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committees, the Chairman, Rajya Sabha
referred the MSMED (Amendment) Bill, 2018 (Annexure-I) on the 01st October, 2018 as introduced in
the Lok Sabha on the 23rd July, 2018 for examination and Report within 3 months.
3. The Committee in its meeting held on the 09th October, 2018 decided to invite the Experts on the
subject and the Stakeholders/Associations concerned to hear their opinion/views/suggestions on the
proposed Amendment.
4. The Committee heard the views of Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and the
Ministry of Law & Justice (Legislative Department) on the Amendment Bill.
5. The Committee held four sittings during the course of examination of the Bill i.e., on 01st, 09th
& 16th November and 27th December, 2018. The list of witnesses heard by the Committee is at
Annexure-II.
6. The Committee has relied on the following documents in finalizing the Report:
(i) The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2018;
(ii) Presentation, clarification and oral evidence of Secretary, M/o MSME;
(iii) Oral evidence and written submissions by various Stakeholders/Experts on the Bill;
(iv) Replies received from the M/o MSME to the Questions/Queries raised by the Members
during the course of the meetings on the Bill; and
(v) Clarifications received from Legislative Department, (M/o Law & Justice).
7. The Committee considered the draft Report and adopted the same on 27th December, 2018.
8. On behalf of the Committee, I would like to acknowledge with thanks the contributions made by
those who deposed before the Committee and also those who gave their suggestions to the Committee
through their written submissions.

printed in bold letters in the Contents of the Reports.
