16. During the course of discussion on Demands for Grants (2020-21) pertaining to the Ministry 
of MSME, the Committee also heard the views of the Representatives of some  Associations from 
Industrial and MSME Sectors like FICCI and FISME. However, ASSOCHAM could not participate 
in the discussion but submitted its written response to the Committee. The Committee appreciates 
and is thankful to the Industry and MSME Associati ons.  Some important and meaningful 
points/suggestions were also shared by the Industry Associations.  
17. The Committee was apprised that the Budget does take a few steps towards addressing the 
decelerating growth rate, specifically in the areas of Govern ance, Export -Import Promotion, and 
Ease of Doing Business etc. for the Industry and Business. The Associations also acclaimed the 
Vivad se Viswas  tax facilitation scheme, increasing audit limits to five crore rupees, allowing 
NBFCs to participate in Bill discounting over the TReDS platform and financing working capital 
requirements through quasi-equity subordinate debts. 
18. The Committee was also apprised by the Associations that even after the government 
issuing policy guidelines, the guidelines are not followed. Most of the Banks do not give the benefit 
of CGTMSE to the MSMEs and insist on collateral security and harassment of the small 
entrepreneurs is a common thing without even giving opportunity and also with no justification. 
Accordingly, they suggested that officers dealing with financial matters and regulatory affairs be 
made more accountable and be allowed to support the MSMEs.  
19. It was also informed by the representatives of MSME Associations that the GST Act need to 
be simplified further for easy application, improvement and allow corrections of genuine mistakes 
and rate rationalization should be applied by the Government. MSMEs always  run on short of 
resources and GST and its maintenance have made MSMEs completely occupied with its processes 
and the returns. Besides, the Committee was also informed that MSMEs need to have separate GST 
registration in each state. As a result, even if th ey have limited or nil business in that State, they 
need to file return which is in totality a very tedious task for a unit who already lack resources. It 
was accordingly suggested that MSMEs should be allowed to have only one unified GST 
registration which is applicable in all states.  
20. Further, the Committee was informed by the representatives of the MSME Associations that 
though the products of Indian MSMEs have the immense potential in global markets,  the Indian 

6 
 
MSMEs are not able to export their go ods as per their true potential due to lack of resources and 
knowledge. Besides, they also do not have enough resources to have a dedicated research team to 
develop the products as per the demand of a certain region or country. In this regard, the 
representatives of MSME Associations suggested to set up an exclusive „Export Facilitation Centre‟ 
for MSMEs to promote exports of products and services from MSME sector. The centre can be 
established in each State with the cooperation of the State government, whi ch could be One Point 
Contact for export facilitation. 
Demands for Grants (2020-21) 
21. The Ministry of MSME informed the Committee while making presentation on the DFG 
(2020-21) that MSMEs provide employment to about 11.10 crore people and contribute around 
28.9% to the country‟s GDP. The Committee was also apprised that under PMEGP (till 15.02.2020) 
around 43,426 micro enterprises have been assisted and about 3.47 lakh employment opportunities 
have been created. Further, the Ministry apprised that the one -time cap of Rs. 200 lakh is removed 
and the borrower can avail incremental credit facil ities now under CGTMSE and so far 39.28 lakh 
guarantees have been approved with coverage of Rs.2.06 lakh crores under the Scheme. To add, it 
was apprised that the corpus to the Credit Guarantee Fund has been enhanced to Rs. 7,500 crores to 
ensure payment to the Banks in case the loan amount becomes NPA.  
22. The Committee was informed by the representatives of MSME Associations that many 
of the MSMEs were unable to meet the fixed deadline of 90 days in repaying their loan 
installments, due to the unique sys tem of their working cycle, which is much longer, due to 
their inability to meet the stipulated timeline for repayment, the MSMEs units are declared 
NPAs. To avoid such difficulties being faced by MSMEs, the Committee recommends that the 
Ministry should en deavor to see to it that time limit for declaring a MSME as NPA due to 
non-payment of loan amount should be enhanced from the current 90 days to 180 days. 
Dream of Five Trillion Dollar Economy and the MSME Sector 
23. The Economic Survey 2018 -19 and the Uni on Budget 2019 -20 have indicated the goal of 
making India a US$ 5 trillion economy by 2024 -25. MSMEs are widely spread across the country 
in all the sectors and the current size of Indian Economy is around $3 trillion in which MSMEs ‟ 
share is estimated to be around $0.9 trillion based on its share of around 30% in the GDP.   
24. In order to increase the contribution of MSMEs in India‟s GDP and to achieve the target of 
$2 trillion mark for MSME sector by 2024 -25, Government is focusing on the key factors of 

7 
 
economic growth i.e. Investment and Productivity (efficiency) and the main parameters of the 
MSME Strategy is:  
(i) investment in all the vertical of MSME Ecosystem viz. human capital, knowledge 
dissemination, access to finance, technology, infrastructure, mar kets, policy, governance 
and ease of doing business. 
(ii) consolidation and convergence of all the MSME related activities under Central/ State 
management 
(iii)exploring the possibility of crowd sourcing of knowledge services and capital to 
supplement the efforts of the Government.  
(iv) implementing projects with external aid from World Bank, ADB etc. to supplement the 
investment of Government of India.  
(v) strengthening linkages of large manufacturing and services sector with micro, small and 
medium enterprises (MSMEs) and  developing a firm value chain within and across the 
sectors.  
(vi) upgrading the rural and urban livelihoods into enterprises by providing them with access 
to capital and market. This will not only lead to formalization of these sectors but also 
capture their contribution in the GDP which is at present either remains unreported or 
underreported.     
25. The Committee welcomes the Government’s goal of making India a $5 trillion 
economy by 2024 -25. The Committee is however of the considered view that the target o f 
becoming $5 trillion economy by 2024 can be achieved by exponential growth of MSME 
sector. This sector has the capacity of building up at a low cost and utilizing the modern 
innovative technology can be made commercially productive at lower cost. This se ctor has 
also the capacity to generate employment and multiplication of production is far easy than the 
big industries.  The Committee , therefore, recommends that Government need to play a 
proactive and constructive role in promoting MSME S ector. More than ease of doing 
business, there is need of creating ease of running business. More information dissemination 
regarding the export requirements should be taken care of. Financial institutions should be 
proactive, friendly and forthcoming. Gov ernment regulators should do handholding and play 
the role of mentors. Besides, change in the attitude of the Government regulators will 
immensely help the MSME S ector. Together with the industry, skilled manpower and the 
support of government authorities, the desired target can be achieved.   
26. Artificial Intelligence is a rapidly emerging concept in the market across the globe , 
which has great potential for enterprises. Most of the entrepreneurs are making use of this 
concept for their benefit and to in crease their outreach.  The Committee recommends that 
Ministry of MSME should also explore th e concept of AI for strengthening and betterment of 
MSME Sector in the country.    

8 
 
27. Market Intelligence plays a crucial role in strengthening and improving the e nterprises. A 
dedicated market intelligence cell is very essential to gather information about latest trends, taste 
and other aspects of the market. It is imperative to keep an eye on International markets and 
MSMEs of developed countries for knowledge of latest technology and developments and to adopt 
good practices prevailing in the developed markets across the globe for benefit of indigenous 
MSMEs. The Committee, therefore, recommends  that a Market Intelligence Cell for MSMEs 
should be set up that would regularly map specific markets, foreign as well as domestic, for 
meeting the requirement of specific MSME clusters and accordingly provide information and 
training to them about consumer preferences, product specifications, technological 
developments and trade agreements. 
28. Taking into consideration the views expressed by some of MSME Associations during 
the course of examination of DFG (2020 -21), the Committee also perceives that a lot of 
reforms on the Tax front too need to be taken to promote and encou rage the MSMEs. The 
Committee accordingly, is of the view that tax rates for proprietary and partnership firms 
should be reduced from 30% to at least 22% on the lines of reduction in Corporate Tax. 
Likewise, exemption and relief under Capital Gain should b e accorded to MSMEs for 
investment in expansion of the existing MSME or for fulfilling their working capital 
requirements. The Committee accordingly, desires that Ministry of MSME may take up these 
issues with the Ministry of Finance and apprise the Committee of the outcome thereof. 
29. The Committee recommends that MSMEs should be allowed to have only one unified 
GST registration , which is applicable in all states. With respect to the sharing of Taxes 
between Central and State Governments, it should be don e at the back end as the 
Government already has all the information in this regard.  
30. The Committee recommends that multiple registrations with multiple government 
agencies for various purposes should be done away with for MSMEs. Inter -Ministries 
coordination should be improved to bring out one registration to carry out all business 
activities including exports, tax and day -to-day business activities to improve ease of doing 
business for MSMEs.  
31. The Committee recommends that Ministry should play a pr oactive role in promoting 
MSMEs abroad and the foreign entrepreneurs should have profiles of Indian MSMEs so that 
they could promote them at appropriate level amongst companies of their respective country. 

9 
 
There should be an exclusive ‘Export Facilitation Centre’ for MSMEs in PPP mode in each 
State to promote exports of products and services from MSME sector.  
32. The Committee observes that there have been instances of inadequate credit 
disbursement by banks to MSMEs vis-à-vis large industries whereas the case should have 
been opposite. In Economic Survey 2018 -19, it has been stated that MSME sector has vast 
potential and it should be nurtured fully to convert dwarfs into the giants. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry s hould take up the matter with the Ministry of Finance and 
RBI to ensure that there is no inadequacy of funds to MSMEs.                             
Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) 
33. The KVIC is entrusted with the functions to plan, promote organize and assist in the 
implementation of the programme by financing the eligible units in Khadi and Village Industries 
sector, imparting training for the employment, ensuring supply of raw materials to the 
units/entrepreneurs, promotion of sales of Kha di and Village Industries products and undertaking 
research and development activities for the growth and spread of Khadi and Village Industries to 
promote the sale and marketing of Khadi or products of Village Industries or handicrafts by forging 
links wi th established marketing agencies wherever possible; and to encourage and promote 
research in technology used in Khadi and VI, including use of non -conventional energy and electric 
power with a view to increasing productivity. The programmes of the KVIC ar e implemented 
through its Regional/States level Offices and State Boards (KVIBs).  The KVIBs implement about 
90% of VI programmes and receive funds from both KVIC and State Governments.  Khadi Sector 
programme in its entirety and a small part of Village In dustries programmes are being implemented 
by KVIC directly.  Both the KVIC and KVIB are promotional bodies which extend a network of 
institutional, infrastructural and financial support to Khadi and Village Industries units/institution.  
34. In response to  a query regarding the future plans of the Ministry for the Khadi Sector and the 
suggestions for the betterment of Khadi Sector, the  Ministry informed that the Khadi Gramodyog Vikas 
Yojana (KGVY) has been implemented during 2019-20 and assistance is provided under various components 
viz., Modified Market Development Assistance (MMDA) to the Khadi Institutions and Khadi Artisans, 
Interest Subsidy Eligibility Certificate (ISEC) Scheme, ensuring availability of working capital to Khadi 
Institutions, Work-shed Scheme for providing sufficient space and congenial environment to Khadi artisans, 
Strengthening of Weak Khadi Institutions, assistance for modernization of sales outlets of Khadi 
Institutions, marketing component for promoting sales and marketing, assista nce under science & 
technology for developing new technologies, and training to the artisans. The Ministry also informed that 

10 
 
the social welfare schemes like Janashree Bima Yojana etc., are implemented for the artisans. Also, to make 
Khadi a youthful and g lobal brand, it is proposed to set up design houses to introduce new and vibrant 
designs.  
35. Regarding the export performance of KVIC/Coir Board, the Committee was apprised that  KVIC do 
not involve directly in the export activities of KVI products. The K VI products are being exported by KVIs 
directly or through merchant/agencies. Moreover, the targets for export are not fixed because export is 
demand driven. However, KVIC participates with Khadi and Village Industry Institutions/units in the 
International Exhibitions organized by different organizations like ITPO, FIEO, TEXPROCIL and other 
Government bodies in different countries. On the other hand, Coir Board has an exclusive export market 
promotion wing for promotion of coir exports. It facilitates coir entrepreneurs to register as coir exporter, 
participation in exhibitions abroad, availing assistance under International co -operation scheme and other 
trade-related matters. Recent research and development activities of Coir Board have made some 
remarkable breakthrough in the development of new products and end user applications of coir. The coir 
pith products are now widely used abroad for agriculture/horticulture applications due to the R&D efforts 
of Coir Board.  
36. It was informed that considering the new trend of e -commerce, new initiatives have been 
undertaken by the KVIC by signing Agreement with Paytm Mall and Aarmart Ecommerce for the 
promotion and marketing support of products produced by the KVI Institutions/Units. Recently 
KVIC had taken the ini tiative for launching exclusive e-commerce platform for marketing the 
products of Khadi and Village Industries through PPP model. 
37. The Committee notes that the constraints faced by KVIC/KVIB are mainly due to 
procedural delays, inadequate technology up-gradation, under utilization of funds etc. Despite 
providing technical guidance to the units in KVI, the problems of the units remain 
inadequately addressed, as a result there is suboptimal functioning of institutions/units and 
high drop outs among new entrants and low employment generation.  The Committee, 
therefore, recommends that KVIC, in view of the expansion of its area of operation in every 
nook and corner of the country, should come forward with a more holistic and unified policy 
in co-ordination with all the stakeholders. Proper planning, monitoring and implementation 
in each scheme are required to meet the primary objective of employment generation.  
38. The Committee feels that in face of stiff competition in the market from organized 
industries, KVIs should concentrate more on adoption of newer technology and upgradation of 
existing technology for products upgradation.  The Committee , therefore, recommends that 

11 
 
regular training by efficient staff having experience and expertise should be imparted  to the 
artisans through its network of training institutions.   
39. The Committee was apprised about the availability of Khadi Fabrics in private retail 
stores at competitive price.  The Committee observes that opening up of Khadi retailing to 
private players is a good initiative in this regard for enhancing and expanding the market of 
Khadi fabrics among the customers. Further, the recent innovative step to bring in fashion 
designers of repute to design Khadi fabrics is a welcome move and it needs to be c ontinued by 
bringing in more such steps.  The Committee , therefore, recommends that good market 
techniques like frequent awareness campaigns among the youth and introduction of Khadi in 
Schools, Hospitals, Railways and other Government Organizations could b e good recourse , 
which will surely increase the demand for Khadi products. Besides, premier showrooms 
known as Khadi Lounge should be opened in all the State capitals and Airports to market 
designer Khadi products and attract the younger generations towards Khadi products. In this 
direction opening up of Designer Houses in each state capitals would be a welcome step.  
40. The Committee observes that the rural as well as urban youths are not  inclined to work in 
KVI sector due to low wages and the hardships i nvolved in it. Therefore, the Committee is of the 
view that the economic empowerment of the poor artisans can be enhanced by allowing the 
potential spinners and weavers to work with the private designers of national and 
international reputation without the  approval of KVIC so that they could earn more wages 
from them directly.  Further, the issue of low wages of unskilled and semi -skilled artisans 
needs to be addressed properly so that more willing workers will bring in more quality output 
in Khadi sector.  
41. It was observed by the Committee that opportunities of export of products of Khadi and 
Village Industries are not yet exploited optimally and the government has to lay emphasis upon the 
exports of KVI products . The Committee recommends that ample facilitation, incentives, less 
compliances, easy and cheaper funds, etc. should be adopted by the Government to encourage 
KVIs/MSMEs to go for exports. Besides, seminars and workshops in clusters should be 
organised to  educate KVIs/MSMEs about opportunities of their products in global market 
and benefits of exports. Besides an e-portal can be designed where the MSME exporters can 
post their applications for clearance or for export facilitation like stuffing/de -stuffing and the 
exporter should also post the date when the actual work will be undertaken.

42. During the consideration of Demands 2020 -21, it was informed by the Ministry that 
PMEGP is a credit linked s ubsidy scheme and aimed at generating self -employment opportunities 
through establishment of micro -enterprises in the non -farm sector by helping traditional artisans 
and unemployed youth. General category beneficiaries can avail margin money subsidy of 25 % of 
the project cost in rural areas and 15 % in urban areas. For beneficiaries belonging to special 
categories such as scheduled caste/scheduled tribe/women the margin money subsidy is 35 % in 
rural areas and 25 % in urban areas. The maximum cost of project i s.Rs. 25 lakh in the 
manufacturing sector and.Rs.10 lakh in the service sector.

Level. The scheme is being implemented through all Public Sector Banks, selected private sector 
banks and co -operative banks. Under the scheme, loan is being provided by banks and the margin 
money subsidy is being provided by Ministry of MSME thro ugh KVIC to micro entrepreneurs in 
the country for setting up of Village Industries.

Scheme of Funds for Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI) 
64. The Committee was informed that KVIC is implementing centrally sponsored scheme 
known as Revamped Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI) to make 
the traditional industries more productive, competitive and to facilitate for their sustainable 
development. It is basically a cluster development programme, designed to pr otect and preserve the 
arts and crafts of rural traditional artisans, in a cluster-based manner. The objective of the scheme is 
to organize traditional industries and artisans into clusters to make them competitive and provide 
support for their long -term s ustainability, sustained employment to enhance marketability of 
products of such clusters, to equip traditional artisans of the associated clusters with the improved 
skills, to make provision for common facilities and improved tools and equipment for artis ans, to 
strengthen the cluster governance systems with the active participation of the stakeholders and to 

19 
 
build up innovative products, improved technologies, advanced processes, market intelligence and 
new models of public-private partnerships. 
65. The Scheme covers three types of interventions: 
(i)   Soft interventions - Activities to build general awareness, counseling, skill   
      development & capacity building, exposure visits, market development initiatives, design 
and product development, etc. 
 (ii)  Hard interventions - Creation of common facility centers, raw material banks,    
        upgradation of production infrastructure, warehousing facilities, tools and     
        technological upgradation, etc. 
   (iii) Thematic interventions - Interventions on a cross-cutting basis for brand building,    
          new media marketing, e-commerce initiatives, research and development, etc. 
 
66. The financial assistance provided for any specific project shall be subject to a maximum of 
Rs. 5 crore to support Soft, Hard and Thematic interventions. 
67. The scheme is implemented through registered implementing agencies. Financial assistance 
is given for Khadi and Village Industries Institutions to create Common Facility Centres (CFCs) 
and new infrastructure, to purchase machinery, equipment, Charkha, Looms and tools, to construct 
Workshed, renovate sales outlets, to ensure Skill development of artisans and also to facilitate 
computer and computer related design, etc. Till December, 2019, 63 clusters were assisted and an 
additional 50 clusters are likely to be approved by March, 2020.  Further, 54 are functional 
benefitting 38970 artisans. The Ministry has so far approved 191 proposals for setting up clusters 
and approved an amount of Rs. 408.19 crores  as grant for implementation of clusters since 2015 -16 
to 2019-20 (till December, 2019). 
68. As per revised guidelines pattern of financial assistance, Rs. 2.50 crore is granted for regular 
Clusters (up to 500 artisans) and Rs. 5.00 crore is granted for ma jor Clusters (more than 500 
artisans). The financial assistance provided for any specific project shall be subject to a maximum 
of Rs. 5 crore.

85. The Coir Board is a statutory body established under the Coir Board Industry Act, 1953 for 
promoting overall development of the coir industry and improving the living conditions of the 
workers engaged in this traditional industry. The activities of the  Board for development of coir 
industries, inter  alia include undertaking scientific, technological and economic research and 
development activities; collecting statistics relating to exports and internal consumption of coir and 
coir products; developing n ew products and designs; organizing publicity for promotion of exports 
and internal sales; marketing of coir and coir products in India and abroad; preventing unfair 
competition between producers and exporters; assisting the establishment of units for manu facture 
of the products; promoting co -operative organization among producers of husks, coir fiber, coir 
yarn and manufactures of coir products; ensuring remunerative returns to producers and 
manufacturers, etc. Production of coir fiber was 5,67,000 MT up t o December,2019 against the

Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) with necessary handholding support by the Coir 
Board through its field offices.  The financial assistance for proc urement of machinery/equipment 
can be obtained under PMEGP scheme for setting up of new coir units for which the maximum 
project cost is Rs. 25 Lakhs. 
99. During the year 2019-20, i.e. up to 31.12.2019, the Board has imparted training to 1416 Coir 
Artisans in spinning of Coir Yarn and manufacturing of value added products and during the 
remaining period, the Board has proposed to train 784 artisans under the scheme.  

28 
 
100. “Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana” is one of the schemes implemented under the  
umbrella scheme of Coir Vikas Yojana.  Under Mahila Coir Yojana, women candidates are 
imparted with training on spinning of coir yarn and on successful completion of the training, 
financial assistance is granted for procurement of ratts/coir processing eq uipments.  The scheme is 
implemented through the field training centers of Coir Board.  Under the Scheme of Skill 
Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana, training is also imparted on manufacture of Value Added 
Products.   
101. The Committee notes that  organizations like Coir Board are providing training on 
various aspects of production and development of new/innovative products.  One of the most 
important objectives of the implementation of various Schemes under Coir Board is the 
employment generation especially in rural areas. The Committee, therefore, recommends that 
Ministry of MSME should give a consideration for recognition of such training 
courses/training institutions so that younger generation will be attracted to such training for 
gainful employment. 
102. Deforestation is one of the major threats for the maintenance of ecological balance. 
The Committee, in order to avoid grave threats which are endangering the climatic conditions 
and human life, recommends that the production of substitutes for w ood, such as coir wood, 
has to be encouraged and more coir clusters under SFURTI have to be established to meet the 
demands of coir -based furnishings and building materials from the domestic as well as 
international market. To achieve this, more funds shou ld be allocated by the Ministry of 
MSME to the Coir Board.  
103. The Committee is of the firm opinion that in order to have a better co -ordination for 
export promotion of coir and its by -products for aiding in multifarious activities such as soil 
erosion c ontrol, landscaping, river embankment etc., tie -ups with Indian Missions abroad 
may be explored.  
104. The Committee is aware that, there are various schemes implemented by the 
Government under which technology developed is transferred to the beneficiaries without any 
charges. The Committee therefore, is of the view that the technology developed by the Coir 
Board should be transferred to entrepreneurs, traders, clusters etc. free of cost to encourage 
potential entrepreneurs to get into the coir sector business.  Besides, steps should also be taken 
to explore the potential overseas markets for export of coir products particularly innovative 
coir products. The Committee is also of the opinion that Buyer -Seller meets and Vendor 

29 
 
Development Programmes may be organized overseas to popularize Indian coir products and 
to tap the virgin overseas markets.  
Micro & Small Enterprises - Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP) 
105. The Ministry of MSME has adopted the Cluster Development approach as a key strategy for 
enhancing the productivity and competitiveness as well as capacity building of Micro and Small 
Enterprises (MSEs) and their collectives in the country. A cluster is a group of enterprises located 
within an identifiable and as far as practicable, contiguous ar ea or a value chain that goes beyond a 
geographical area and producing same/similar products/complementary products/services, which 
can be linked together by common physical infrastructure facilities that help address their common 
challenges.  
106. The mai n objective is to support the sustainability and growth of MSEs by addressing 
common issues such as improvement of technology, skills & quality, market access etc.; to build 
capacity of MSEs for common supportive action through formation of self help group s, consortia, 
upgradation of associations etc.; to create/upgrade infrastructural facilities in the new/existing 
Industrial Areas/Clusters of MSEs; to set up Common Facility Centres (for testing, training, raw 
material depot, effluent treatment, complement ing production processes, etc); and promotion of 
green & sustainable manufacturing technology for the clusters so as to enable units switch to 
sustainable and green production processes and products. 
107. The scheme supports financial assistance for establishment of common facility centres 
(CFCs) and to create/upgrade infrastructural facilities (IDs) in the new/existing industrial 
areas/clusters of MSEs. As far as the government grant is concerned CFCs, it is restricted to 70% of 
the cost of Project o f maximum Rs. 20.00 crore.  However, the grant will be 90% for CFCs in 
North-East & Hilly States, Island territories; Aspirational Districts/LWE affected Districts; Clusters 
with more than 50% micro/ village, women owned, and SC/ST units. 
108. Further, the Ministry informed that u nder the MSE-CDP, 1421 potential clusters have been 
identified by field establishments of Office of DC (MSME) namely MSME - Development 
Institutes, across the country. The project proposals along with the Detailed Project Reports (D PRs) 
are required to be forwarded by respective State Governments in respect of these identified clusters 
to office of DC (MSME). Ministry of MSME would accord necessary approvals for the submitted 
proposals and provide financial assistance for setting up of Common Facility Centres (CFCs) under 
the MSE -CDP subject to availability of budgetary provision. The Steering Committee under the 

30 
 
Chairmanship of Secretary, MSME is the Apex Body to sanction and monitor progress of MSE -
CDP. 
109. The Committee is of the view that Micro & Small Enterprises - Cluster Development 
Programme is quite important for the growth and development of Micro and Small 
Enterprises in the country for employment generation and economic development. The 
Scheme, therefore, should never ever  suffer due to paucity of funds. The Committee 
recommends that more budgetary provisions should be made under the scheme so that its 
objectives are achieved. Further, for development of Clusters, state governments should be 
sensitized for timely clearance of procedural matters so that target is achieved.  
Procurement and Market Support (PMS) Scheme 
110. Procurement and Market Support  Scheme has been revamped to enhance the marketability 
of products and services in the MSME Sector. The objective is to promot e new market access 
initiatives, create awareness and educate the MSMEs about various relevant marketing aspects and 
development marketability. Under the scheme, various types of assistance available are: 
participation of individual MSEs in domestic trade fairs/exhibition across the country; 
organizing/participation in trade fairs/exhibitions (Regional/National/International by the 
Ministry/Office of DC (MSME)/Government organizations); capacity building of MSMEs in 
modern packaging technique; development o f marketing Haats; international/national 
workshops/seminars; State Level Vendor Development Programmes (SLVDP) and National Level 
Vendor Development Programme (NLVDP); and  Awareness programmes. 
111. Further, the Ministry apprised that International Coope ration (IC) Scheme is a demand 
driven scheme under which financial assistance is provided on reimbursement basis to the 
Central/State Government organisations, registered industries associations/organisations and 
societies/trusts associated with developmen t and promotion of MSME Sector. Under this scheme, 
eligible organisations are facilitated for visit/participation of MSMEs in International 
exhibitions/trade fairs/buyer -seller meets etc. abroad and also for holding international 
conferences/seminars/workshops in India, for technology infusion, exploring business 
opportunities, joint ventures etc.  An amount of Rs.20.00 crores has been earmarked in BE 2020 -
2021 and the estimated targets are assisting 800 entrepreneurs and holding 50 international 
fairs/exhibitions. 
112. In response to a query regarding the new initiatives that have been undertaken in the development 
of Marketing Infrastructure for Khadi products in view of the growing competition in the market due to the 

31 
 
presence of big e -commerce players like Flipkart, Amazon etc ., the Ministry informed that  considering the 
new trend of e-commerce, initiatives have been undertaken by the KVIC by signing Agreement with Paytm 
Mall and Aarmart Ecommerce for the promotion and marketing support of KVI products produced by the 
KVI Institutions/Units. Recently, KVIC had taken the initiative for launching exclusive                 e-commerce 
platform for marketing the products of Khadi and Village Industries through PPP model. 
113. For a successful business, a succ essful marketing strategy  from market research is required for 
making profit and achieving the overall objectives of the organization  in the present scenario. However, 
the Committee observes that the budgetary allocations made under the Marketing Promotion  Scheme 
for the FY 2020 -21 is Rs. 103.63 crores which is less than what was allocated for the previous year. The 
Committee, therefore, recommends that more funds be allocated for the purpose at the Revised 
Estimates stage so that marketing promotion aspect does not suffer due to lack of funds.  
Science & Technology (S&T) 
114. Khadi and Village Industries Commission has been functioning with the vision of boosting 
and injecting innovation, quality and productivity to make the Khadi and Village Industries 
products globally competitive and also to enable rural industries get its due to market demand. In 
this regard, KVIC has made strong effort to address the Quality aspect, Research and Development 
need of KVI Sector through Research and Development (R&D) proje cts, ISO Certification and 
Total Quality Management (TQM). Research and Development activities are continuously explored 
and implemented in the areas of technology by providing scientific inputs to needy institutions with 
an objective to increase the produ ctivity and quality of the product through reputed Scientific 
Institutions. During the year 2018 -19, 14 Khadi Projects and 12 Village Industries Projects were 
assisted under Science & Technology. Also , in 2019-20 (Up to 31.12.2019), 6 Khadi Projects were 
assisted under Science & Technology programme.  
115. Today‟s age is the age of Science & Technology.  Science & Technology has become an 
integral part of our life and life without it is unimaginable now.  The Committee recommends that 
with changing time and scenario, the Science & Technology aspect should be focused upon 
more in order to benefit the Khadi and Village Industries Sector.  The Ministry may ensure 
that suitable technology and research being practiced in the other developed MSME Sector s 
across the world be incorporated suitably for indigenous MSMEs.  
116. The Committee recommends that Ministry must encourage MSMEs for innovation 
and R&D, provide adequate institutional support for encouraging innovation, provide special 
support, both tech nical & financial, to innovators to set up enterprises for scientific & 

32 
 
technological R&D  purposes to make indigenous MSMEs more competitive in the world 
market vis-a-vis MSMEs of the developed countries. The Ministry must also ensure that 
budgetary allocations are fully utilized for the intended purposes.  
117. The Committee recommends that Ministry may tie up with different research 
organizations, both in government as well as private sector, for R&D of scientific & 
technological activities of KVIC and Co ir Board. Besides, exhibitions, Seminars, Workshops, 
Awareness programmes/road shows all over India may be organized. Incubation & intensive 
training on the latest technologies developed should be imparted to the industry/beneficiaries 
free of cost or on nominal fee. The Committee desires that the Ministry may pursue with right 
earnest to put in place a network of incubators in the entire length & breadth of the country 
to enhance the competitiveness of the MSMEs. 
118. R&D is an important aspect of any ente rprise. In developed countries, proper and 
dedicated R&D is undertaken to improve the quality of products and performance of the 
enterprises. However, for 2020-21, a meager amount of Rs. 2.00 crore has been earmarked for 
R&D purposes. The Committee recomme nds that more funds should be allocated for R&D 
and Technology related support facilities in order to match the quality of international 
products.

Public Procurement Policy 
140. The Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises (PPP-MSE) Order 2012 has 
mandated that every Central Ministry/Department/PSU shall set an annual goal for procurement 
from the MSE sector at the beginning of the year, with the objective of achi eving an overall 
procurement goal of minimum 25 per cent of the total annual purchases from the products or 
services produced or rendered by MSEs, with sub-targets of 4 per cent for SC/ST-owned MSEs, and 
3 per cent for women -owned MSEs. The SAMBANDH portal  shows the procurement from the 
MSEs by the CPSEs as per the PPP-MSE Order, 2012 provisions.  
141. Further, it was informed by the Ministry that there is provision of Tender sets free of cost 
and exemption from payment of earnest money to registered MSEs. MSEs quoting price within 
price band L -1 + 15%, when L1 is from someone other than MSE, shall be allowed to supply at 
least 25% of tendered value at L -1 subject to lowering of price by MSEs to L -1. 358 items are 
reserved for exclusive procurement from MSEs . For enhancing participation of MSEs in 
government procurement, Ministry/Department/CPSUs shall conduct Vendor Development 
Programmes or Buyer Seller Meets for MSEs especially for SC/ST entrepreneurs. 
142. On the effectiveness of the MSME “SAMBANDH PORTAL” in monitoring the settlement 
of payments to MSEs under the Public Procurement Policy, the Ministry of MSME apprised that 
SAMADHAAN PORTAL was launched on 30 th October, 2017 to enable Micro & Small 
Enterprises (MSEs) across the country to directly register their cases online on the portal relating to 
delayed payments by Central Ministries/Departments/CPSEs/State Government etc. The 
information about the pending payments from Central Ministries/Departments/CP SEs/State 

38 
 
Government etc., and other buyers are available in public domain and can be viewed by the MSEs 
or any member of the public.  Further, it was informed that since inception till date , around 8028 
disputes have been registered and out of that 459 di sputes have been disposed off through the 
portal. 
143. In a visit of the Committee  to Kolkata, Hyderabad and Mumbai in January, 2020 , it 
came to the notice that although the CPSEs have made payments to the MSEs but still the 
portal showed pendency against the concerned CPSEs due to lack of updation of information 
on the Portal . The Committee recommends that a proper monitoring mechanism should be 
put in place to check such type of information on the SAMADHAAN portal and data about 
the payments made should be regularly updated and errors must be rectified immediately. 
144. The Committee also observes that the procurements by the CPSEs from the SC/ST and 
Women entrepreneurs, as mandated under the Public Procurement Policy, are much below 
than the sub-quota of 4% and 3% respectively. Even many of the CPSEs have not organized 
Vendor Development Programmes (VDPs) to sensitize the SC/ST entrepreneurs. The 
Committee recommends that sufficient number of VDPs be organized along with buyer -seller 
meets for the benefit of SC/ST and Women entrepreneurs. 
145. Since delayed payments to MSEs have been a longstanding issue, the  Committee also 
recommends that more MSEFC should be constituted in all the states to resolve the problem 
of delayed payments expeditiously. Besides, the MSEs should be made aware of the benefits of 
the newly introduced TReDS Platform, wherein bills are paid on a fast track basis. 
146. The Committee is of the view that the Government Purchase scheme may be amended 
so as to reduce the PBG/secur ity deposit requirement to 10% for Micro Enterprises, 20% for 
Small Enterprises and 30% for Medium Enterprises compared to the PBG required from 
non-MSMEs. It is also suggested that Medium Industry should also be granted the 
preferential procurement facility and to pay 25% of the EMD/Bid Bond & tender charges as 
specified in the tenders. Besides, priority sector lending target for micro enterprises from 
current 7.5% of Adjusted Net Bank Credit may be enhanced to at least 12%.

reduced against BE of Rs. 232.00 crore in year 2018 -19. To consi der ASPIRE an important 
and crucial scheme for innovative entrepreneurship in agro -industry, the Committee is , 
however disappointed to note that only an amount of Rs. 30 crore has been proposed for 2020-
21. The Committee, therefore, recommends that more bu dgetary provisions should be made 
for such an important scheme. Apart from  this, steps may be taken to restructure the Scheme

to implement the scheme successfully and meaningfully. 
149. The Committee is of the opinion that Ministry needs to improve employability of 
incubates if the schemes are to succeed. The Committee is also of the opinion that it would be 
better if ASPIRE is closely linked up with MUDRA, Stand Up a nd Start Up Schemes to 
provide financial assistance to the entrepreneurs. Further, the LBIs should tie up with S elf 
Help Groups and women organizations, ITIs and skill development institutions. 
150. The Committee recommends that more LBIs/TBIs should be se t up by the Ministry to

population in general and among potential artisans in parti cular, regarding these LBIs/TBIs

National Small Industries Corporation Ltd. (NSIC) 
154. The Ministry of MSME apprised the Committee that the National Small Industries 
Corporation Ltd. (NSIC) is an ISO 9000 certified company under the Ministry of Micro, Small & 
Medium Enterprises.  NSIC has been working to fulfill its mission of promoting, aid ing and 
fostering the growth of small -scale industries and industry related small -scale services/business in 
the country. Over a period of transition, growth and development, the NSIC has proved its strength 
within the country as well as abroad by providin g integrated support services encompassing 
marketing, finance, modernization and up -gradation of technology, quality consciousness, 
strengthening linkages with large and medium enterprises and enhancing export projects and 
products from small-scale enterprises. 
155. The functions of NSIC are as follows :- 
 To create awareness about technological up-gradation. 
 To develop technology transfer centers and software technology parks. 
 To export the products of small business units in order to develop export worthiness. 
 To obtain, supply and distribute indigenous and imported raw materials. 
 To provide mentoring and advisory services. 
 To serve as technology business incubators.
