necessary, the Ministry should seek additional budgetary allocations at the Revised Estimates 
(RE) stage from the Ministry of Finance to maximize the Scheme’s potential in promotin g 
electric bus adoption and green energy transition.  
(Para 35) 
 
Action Taken Replies 
 
An allocation of Rs.4,391 crore has been made under the PM E -DRIVE Scheme for the 
deployment of 14,028 electric buses (e -buses) by State Transport Undertakings (STUs) an d 
public transport agencies, primarily of nine cities with over 40 lakh population, i.e. Delhi, 
Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Ahmedabad, Surat, Bangalore, Pune, and Hyderabad.  However, 
buses shall also be deployed by STUs in unique geographies like hilly and north-eastern states, 
island territories, coastal regions, etc. on non-OPEX (Operating Expense) model. 
 
It is pertinent to mention that PM -eBusSewa Scheme of the Ministry of Housing and Urban 
Affairs aims to deploy 10,000 e-Buses in cities with population less than 40 lakhs. 
 
As per information posted by Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) on PIB on 13 th  
February,  2025, a total of 7,293 electric buses have been approved for cities across 14 States and 
4 Union Territories (UTs). An amount of ₹983 .75 crore was sanctioned for the development of 
power and civil depot infrastructure, out of which Rs.563.34 crore has been sanctioned for power 
infrastructure in 66 cities and Rs.420.40 crore for civil depot infrastructure in 64 cities. It has 
further been informed that Rs.437.50 crore has been disbursed for the development of power and 
civil infrastructure in 7 States and 1 Union Territory in FY 2024 -25. Therefore, the PM -
eBusSewa Scheme is ensuring e-bus adoption and green energy transition in small cities in India. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
The Committee is of the view that the curre nt deployment of electric buses i.e. 14,028 in 
nine major cit ies and 7,293 for cities across 14 States and 4 Union Territories  is grossly 
inadequate to meet the Government’s declared objective of achieving 30% electric vehicle 
penetration by 2030. Given the urgency of transitioning to clean mobility and the critical 
role of public transport in this shift, the Committee strongly re commends that the Ministry 
immediately pursue enhanced budgetary allocations at the RE stage for 2025 -26. A 

26 
 
substantial scale-up in the deployment of electric buses across both large and small cities is 
imperative to meet national targets, reduce fossil fu el dependency, and address the 
worsening urban air quality across the country. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
12.   The Committee emphasises that charging infrastructure is crucial for successfully 
transitioning to electric mobility. A meagre Rs. 180.00 crore was allocated at the RE stage for 
2024-25 for installing EV public charging stations across the country, and the entire amount 
remains unutilised. It recommends that the Ministry proactively seek enhanced funding from the 
Ministry of Finance at the R E stage (2025 -26) to expedite the installation of charging 
infrastructure under the PM E -DRIVE, thereby providing a much -needed boost to electric 
mobility. 
(Para 38) 
Action Taken Replies 
 
Rs.180 crore were allocated towards installation of EVPCS under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme at 
RE Stage in FY 2024 -25.  However, the total allocation for EV PCS under the Scheme is 
Rs.2,000 crore.  
 
Further, Rs.650 crore has been estimated under Budgeted Estimates for FY 2025 -26 towards 
installation of charging infrastructure as  per Guidelines of Ministry of Power. It is expected that 
in the current FY i.e. 2025 -26, approximately Rs.593 crore shall be spent towards installation of 
EVPCS. 
 
The guidelines on charging infra will be shortly released by MHI for rolling out adequate le vels 
of charging infrastructure. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee notes that although a total outlay of ₹2,000 crore  has been earmarked 
under the PM E -DRIVE Scheme for the installation of Electric Vehicle Public Charging 
Stations (EVPCS), only ₹180 crore was allocated at the RE stage in FY 2024 –25 and 
remained unutilised. While ₹650 crore has been budgeted for FY 2025–26 and ₹593 crore is 
projected to be spent, the Committee is of the view that the pace of allocation and 
utilisation remains misaligned with the overall target. It further observes that delays in 
finalising the charging infrastructure guidelines may impede timely deployment and 
undermine public confidence in EV adoption. 
 
Accordingly, the Committee recommends that the Ministry expedite the issuance of 
comprehensive guidelines for EVPCS and prepare a structured, year -wise implementation 

27 
 
roadmap for the optima l and time -bound utilisation of the ₹2,000 crore corpus. This 
roadmap should include city -wise and corridor -specific targets to ensure equitable and 
demand-driven distribution of charging stations. The Committee also requests to be 
apprised of the projected timeline for full utilisation of the EVPCS allocation under the PM 
E-DRIVE Scheme, along with periodic progress updates to enable effective oversight. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
13. The scheme's budget rose sharply in 2024 -25, but actual expenditure remains below RE, 
highlighting utilisation challenges. For 2025-26, a budget allocation of ₹155.76 crore has been 
proposed. The Committee believes this scheme facilitates realising the goal of Make in India and 
Atmnirbhar Bharat by promoting newer and niche technologies. It needs to be implemented 
promptly and effectively with robust zeal. Therefore, i t is recommended that the scheme's 
implementation be streamlined to ensure efficient fund utilisation, timely disbursement, and 
alignment with industry demand to maximize its impact on domestic battery manufacturing.  
(Para 47) 
 
Action Taken Replies 
 
The PLI ACC Scheme has been und er gestation period till December 2024. Moreover, since the 
Lithium-Ion cell manufacturing technology is a very niche technology, currently not fully 
developed in India, the projects under the PLI ACC Scheme (Round -1) could not meet their pre-
declared timelines in terms of commencement of communicated production.  
  
However, the Ministry of Heavy Industries is organizing monthly workshops with the 
beneficiary firms to monitor progress, ensure efficient fund utilization, timely disbursement and 
alignment with industry demand to maximize its impact on domestic battery manufacturing. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
The Committee notes the delays in project execution under the PLI ACC Scheme, despite 
the Ministry’s efforts through monthly workshops. Given t he strategic importance of 
domestic battery manufacturing for achieving self -reliance, the Committee strongly 
recommends that the Ministry adopt a results -driven approach with clearly defined 
milestones, strict timelines, and accountability mechanisms. Tec hnical support and close 
monitoring must be intensified to ensure timely commencement of production and effective 
utilisation of funds, thereby accelerating progress toward the goals of Make in India and 
Atmanirbhar Bharat. 
 
 

28 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
14. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Heavy Industries implement the recent 
customs duty exemptions on 35 additional capital goods essential for lithium -ion battery 
manufacturing. Given India's reliance on battery imports, particularly from China , and the high 
investment required for ACC production, these exemptions will provide a competitive edge to 
domestic manufacturers. Additionally, their alignment with the PLI ACC scheme is expected to 
boost indigenous manufacturing, reduce import dependence , and enhance India’s position in the 
global EV market.  
(Para 49) 
Action Taken Replies 
 
The Government's recent exemption of customs duties on 35 additional capital goods essential 
for lithium-ion battery manufacturing is poised to significantly impact the automotive industry in 
terms of the use of indigenous advanced chemistry cells. 
 
As Lithium -Ion cell manufacturing technology is a very niche technology, currently not fully 
developed in India, the cell manufacturers are required to invest heavily in t heir facilities 
including investment on import of latest capital goods required for manufacturing of ACCs.  
Due to lack of indigenous sourcing of capital goods, only way to get a competitive edge is by 
exempting customs duties on such critical capital goods. 
 
The duty exemptions complement the PLI ACC Scheme by incentivizing domestic 
manufacturing of ACC technologies. This synergy is anticipated to strengthen India's position in 
the global EV market, making the country's automotive sector more competitive internationally. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
The Committee welcomes the customs duty exemptions on 35 additional capital goods 
critical to lithium -ion battery manufacturing and acknowledges their strategic alignment 
with the PLI ACC Scheme. However,  to fully leverage this policy synergy, the Committee 
recommends that the Ministry ensure swift and seamless implementation of these 
exemptions, along with regular consultations with industry stakeholders to identify any 
procedural bottlenecks. It further urges the Ministry to track and assess the on -ground 
impact of these exemptions on project cost reduction, capacity building, and localization 
efforts. Strengthening this facilitative ecosystem is essential to accelerate the growth of 
indigenous ACC manufacturing and reduce long-term dependency on imports, particularly 
from China. 
 
 
 

29 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
15. The Committee notes the significant changes in the Mines and Minerals ( Development 
and Regulation) [MMD R] Amendment Act, 2023 . The amendments to  the Act enables 
participation of private companies in mining exploration by providing them with exploration 
license for reconnaissance and prospecting of critical minerals. The Committee is hopeful that 
the participation of private players will expedite t he exploration and mining of critical minerals 
like lithium without technological constraints. This is expected to strengthen indigenous 
manufacturing of lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles and reduce dependence on imports of 
critical minerals. 
(Para 50) 
 
Action Taken Replies 
 
As per the information received from the Ministry of Mines, the Ministry of Mines has been 
empowered to auction blocks for grant of Exploration License through an order dated 21 st 
October, 2024 under Section 20A of MMDR Act 1957. Central Government has successfully 
auctioned 24 blocks of critical and strategic minerals in 04 tranches in 2024. 
  
The exploration of critical minerals has been significantly increased. Over the past thr ee years, 
the Geological Survey of India (GSI) has undertaken 368 exploration projects focused on critical 
and strategic minerals. In the FY 2024 -25, 195 projects were taken up, and 227 projects have 
been approved for the financial year 2025-26. 
 
100% FDI is allowed under “Automatic” route for mining and exploration of metal and non -
metal ores. A foreign company may incorporate an Indian subsidiary company or invest in an 
existing Indian Company to become eligible for grant of mining and exploration rights. 
  
To support the critical minerals sector, Government has eliminated customs duties on 25 
minerals and reduced Basic Customs Duties (BCD) on 2 minerals in the Union Budget for 2024 -
25. 
 
In the Union Budget 2025 -26, the Government proposed to fully exempt cobalt powder and 
waste, the scrap of lithium -ion battery, Lead, Zinc and 12 more critical minerals to secure their 
availability for manufacturing in India and promote more jobs for India’s youth. 
  
Ministry of Mines is engaged in various multilateral and bilateral platforms for strengthening the 
critical minerals value chain, focussing on multiple objectives, including the processing and 
recycling of critical minerals such as Minerals Security Partnership (MSP) and the Indo -Pacific 
Economic Framework (IPEF), initiative on Critical and Emerging Technologies (iCET), the UK -
India Technology Security Initiative (TSI) and others. 

30 
 
 The Ministry of Mines has taken a significant step to acquire overseas mineral assets through the 
establishment of a joint venture co mpany, KhanijBidesh India Ltd. (KABIL). Its overarching 
mission is to identify and acquire overseas mineral assets that hold critical and strategic 
significance, specifically targeting minerals like Lithium, Cobalt and others. KABIL has signed 
an Explorati on and Development Agreement with CAMYEN, a state -owned enterprise of 
Catamarca province of Argentina, for Exploration and mining of Five Lithium Brine Block in 
Argentina with an area of around 15,703 Ha. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
The Committee acknowledges the positive developments in enabling exploration through 
private participation, successful auctioning of 24 critical mineral blocks, increased 
exploration projects by GSI, and fiscal measures such as reduction and exemption of 
customs duties on key minerals. It commends the Ministry’s efforts in securing overseas 
lithium assets via KABIL and engaging in international platforms for strategic mineral 
sourcing. 
 
However, the Committee remains concerned about the delayed operationalization of 
auctioned blocks, limited private uptake in high -risk exploration, and domestic refining 
gaps for key minerals like lithium. It recommends that the Ministry prioritize timely 
activation of blocks and strengthen coordination with industry, foreign partners, and  state 
agencies to fast -track exploration, processing infrastructure, and critical asset acquisition 
under platforms like KABIL and the Minerals Security Partnership to ensure long -term 
supply security and reduce reliance on imports. 
 
CENTRAL PUBLIC SECTOR ENTERPRISES (CPSES) 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
16. The Committee observed that out of the 16 Operational CPSEs under the administrative 
control of the Ministry of Heavy Industries, 6 1 CPSEs are loss making CPSEs. It has also been 
observed that HEC is a loss-making enterprise continuously for the past several years. However, 
considering the recent performance of HEC, there seems to be potential for its revival if 
immediate measures are taken. It recommends that the Ministry should make concerted efforts to 
improve the situation of HEC and assess the reasons as to why the loss making CPSEs have 
increased from 5 to 6. The Ministry may develop strategic steps to revive the CPSEs and 
accordingly consider allocating funds at RE stage.  
(Para 64) 
                                                           
1Engineering Projects (India) Limited (EPIL), Heavy Engineering Corporation (HEC), Hindustan Machine Tools 
Ltd. (HMT), Rajasthan Electronics and Instruments Limited (REIL), Andrew Yule & Co. Ltd. (AYCL) and NEPA 
Ltd.  

31 
 
Action Taken Replies 
 
Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) has 16 Operational Central Public Sector Enterprises 
(CPSEs). Out of these, following 5 CPSEs were loss making during FY 2022-23: 
i. Heavy Engineering Corporation Ltd. (HEC) 
ii. HMT Machine Tools Ltd. 
iii. NEPA Ltd. 
iv. Engineering Projects (India) Ltd. 
v. Rajasthan Electronics & Instruments Ltd.  
 
In FY 2023-24, one more Company, namely Andrew Yule & Company Limited (AYCL) became 
loss making CPSE. AYCL is m ainly engaged in growing and manufacturing tea. Due to Pest 
(looper caterpillars) and Fungal (fusarium) attack on Tea plantation, adverse climatic conditions, 
erratic rain falls, low sale realization, etc. in its Tea Division, it registered loss in FY 2023-24. 
 
As regards HEC, its financial health has been poor since long. In recent 3 years, it has registered 
Profit Before Tax as under: 
2021-22 - (-)256.07 Cr 
2022-23 - (-)230.85 Cr 
2023-24 - (-)275.19 Cr 
 
There is no indication for financial revival of the company and there is no significant 
improvement in performance of the company. However, the performance of CPSEs under 
administrative control of this Ministry is periodically reviewed and wherever required, funds 
under RE stage may be considered. 
Further Recommendations/Observations 
The Committee notes that the number of loss -making CPSEs under the administrative 
control of the Ministry has increased from five in FY 2022 –23 to six in FY 2023 –24, with 
Andrew Yule & Company Limited (AYCL) newly added due to a dverse agro -climatic 
conditions affecting its Tea Division. The Committee reiterates its concern over this trend 
and recommends that the Ministry undertake a detailed assessment of the operational and 
financial challenges faced by these CPSEs. Strategic in terventions, including restructuring, 
diversification, and targeted support, should be considered to arrest further deterioration 
and facilitate revival where feasible. 
With respect to Heavy Engineering Corporation Ltd. (HEC), the Committee acknowledges 
the Ministry’s assessment of its prolonged financial stress. However, based on its ongoing 
consultations with stakeholders and experts, the Committee remains optimistic ab out 
identifying viable pathways for HEC’s revival. It recommends that the Ministry actively 

32 
 
engage with the Committee’s deliberations and prepare a time -bound revival strategy, 
including operational reforms and financial restructuring. The Committee furthe r 
recommends that, subject to progress on revival planning, the Ministry may consider 
allocating appropriate support at the RE stage to enable implementation of corrective 
measures. 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
17. The Committee notes that the number of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) 
under the control of the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) is decreasing year after year. The 
Committee recommends that the Ministry work towards enhancing the performance of CPSEs 
under its control and adopt rest ructuring measures to revive the loss -making CPSEs so that no 
further closure of the CPSEs takes place. Since privately run enterprises/industries are thriving, 
the Ministry should analyse the causes of its CPSEs' sickness and loss -making and make 
concerted efforts for their revival/restoration. 
(Para 65) 
 
Action Taken Replies 
 
The observation of Committee is noted. MHI reviews performance of CPSEs under its 
administrative control periodically evaluating performance of the CPSEs on both financial and 
quantitative operating parameters (such as capacity utilization, realization of trade receivables, 
completion of pending orders, physical performance for completion of projects of national 
importance etc.). 
Further Recommendations/Observations 
The Committee observes that, despite the Ministry’s reference to periodic performance 
reviews of CPSEs, it has not provided specific insights into the root causes of sickness or 
the remedial measures being pursued for their revival. The Committee, therefor e, 
recommends that the Ministry should go beyond routine evaluations and undertake a 
comprehensive diagnostic review of each loss -making CPSE under its control. This review 
should clearly identify the structural, operational, or financial issues affecting performance 
and propose a concrete, time-bound revival strategy for each loss-making CPSE. A detailed 
and substantive response on these aspects may be submitted to the Committee in the Action 
Taken Replies. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
18. The Committee having observed that as on 31.01.2025, the actual utilization of funds by 
several Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) through Internal & Extra Budgetary 

33 
 
Resources (IEBR) remains significantly low compared to the Annual Plan for 2024 -25. It  
recommends that the Ministry identify the reasons for this under -utilization and take necessary 
measures to ensure that the funds raised are effectively utilized before the end of the current 
financial year.

should be implemented in a time-bound manner to ensure that future IEBR allocations are

CHAPTER – I 
THE RECOMMENDATIONS / OBSERVATIONS, WHICH HAVE BEEN 
ACCEPTED BY THE MINISTRY  
 
INTRODUCTION 
Recommendation/observation 
 
1. The Committee appreciates the new initiative to issue customized credit cards with a ₹5 lakh 
limit for micro enterprises. It recommends that the Ministry expedite the distribution of these 
cards, focusing on micro enterprises th at are not entirely digitized. Financial literacy 
programs should also be provided to help these businesses effectively utilize the cards, 
improving access to working capital and financial services. 
(Para No. 20) 
 Action Taken Replies  
Department of Financ ial Services (DFS) has informed that the recommendations of the 
Committee have been noted and will be taken up for suitable action during the implementation 
of the customized credit cards. 
 OVERALL BUDGETARY ALLOCATIONS & ISSUES 
 Recommendation/observation 
 
2. With regard to QEP targets set for the Financial Year 2025 -26, the Committee recommends 
that the Ministry apply lessons learned from the previous year by implementing a clear 
Quarterly and Monthly Expenditure Plan to ensure efficient fund utilization. Additionally, the 
Ministry should focus on strengthening initiative planning, execution, and budget absorption 
capacity to guarantee that allocated funds are utilized effectively, driving tangible outcomes in 
MSME initiatives. 
(Para No. 25) 
 Action Taken Replies  
For the financial year 2025 -26, the monthly and quarterly expenditure plans (MEP & QEP has 
been chalked out for effective utilisation of fund in a uniform manner throughout the Financial 
Year, which is tabulated as under :

Recommendation/observation 
 
3. The Committee acknowledges that most schemes are demand -driven, but it recommends that 
the Ministry set clear, predefined targets for these schemes. It recommends utilizing 
behavioural science tools to nudge, encourage, and motivate organizati ons, leading to better 
stakeholder outcomes. 
(Para No. 27)

The Ministry has set monthly and quarterly expenditure target in respect of all the schemes.

SCHEME WISE ANAYLSIS 
Recommendation/observation 

4 
 
4.  The Committee is of the view that given the significant increase in guarantee approvals, 
particularly in the manufacturing sector, it is recommended that CGTMSE focus on continuing 
to strengthen and incentivize the manufacturing sector through enhanced guarantee coverage 
and tailored support. This could include providing additional benefits or financial incentives for 
MSEs in manufacturing, which could help boost industrial output and employment, particularly 
in key sectors driving economic growth. 
(Para No. 42) 
Action Taken Replies  
CGTMSE provides credit guarantee for the credit facilities up to ₹10 crore extended by its MLIs 
to new as well as existing MSEs without collateral security and third -party guarantee f or the 
activities mentioned in the MSMED Act, 2006. 
 CGTMSE provides credit guarantee at liberal terms for MSEs engaged in manufacturing and 
having ZED (Zero Defect Zero Effect) certification i.e concession in fee @ 10% and higher 
guarantee coverage of 85%, thereby facilitating MSEs to become world-class manufacturers. 
Under Credit Guarantee Scheme of the Ministry of MSME, guarantee cover has been increased 
to Rs 10 Crore from Rs 5 Crore w.e.f. 1.04.2025. Further, DFS has launched a Scheme for MSEs 
in manufacturing. 
Recommendation/observation  
5. The Committee acknowledges the remarkable progress made under the PM Vishwakarma 
Scheme, with 2.66 crore applications received and over 27.49 lakh beneficiaries registered 
within just 16 months, already exceeding th e 5 -year target. However, it urges the Ministry to 
build on this success by further expanding the scheme's outreach, ensuring the timely and 
efficient disbursement of loans, and strengthening the marketing and digital support provided to 
artisans. 
(Para No. 46) 
6. The Committee also appreciates the allocation of ₹5,100 crore for FY 2025 -26 to PM 
Vishwakarma Scheme and recommends that the Ministry focus on optimizing the utilization of 
these funds to maximize the scheme’s impact and further benefit artisans. 
(Para No. 47) 
Action Taken Replies  
The Ministry acknowledges the Hon'ble Committee's appreciation of the progress made under 
the PM Vishwakarma Scheme. Efforts are underway to further expand the scheme's outreach 

5 
 
through targeted IEC campaigns at the g rassroots level, focused attention on trades with low 
enrolment, and timely disbursement of loans in coordination with lending institutions and the 
Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance. Additionally, steps are being taken to 
strengthen digital onboarding, enable e -commerce integration, and enhance marketing linkages 
for registered beneficiaries, in collaboration with States and UTs. The Ministry is also ensuring 
doorstep delivery of modern toolkits to all the PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries th rough an e -
voucher-based redemption system via India Post. Efforts are currently underway to ramp up 
toolkit supplies to meet the growing demand. The Ministry remains committed to the optimal 
utilization of allocated funds to maximize the scheme’s impact a nd ensure sustained benefits for 
traditional artisans and craftspeople. 
Recommendation/observation 
7. The Committee commends the success of PMEGP in fostering self -employment and micro -
enterprises, creating over 9.87 lakh businesses. The Committee also rec ommends scaling up the 
program, focusing on rural and Aspirational Districts, while expanding support for women, SCs, 
and STs. 
(Para No.55) 
Action Taken Replies  
1. Under PMEGP, SC/ST, Women and beneficiaries belonging to Aspirational Districts are 
covered under Special category which are eligible for higher subsidy upto 35% of the project 
cost and lower own contribution as compared to General category beneficiaries. Additionally 
own contribution of Special Category Beneficiaries it is only 5% of project co st whereas it is 
10% for General Category. 
2. While conducting awareness programmes, webinars, workshops, etc., more emphasis is given 
to rural, backward, under -served areas and Aspirational districts particularly for SC/ST, women 
beneficiaries. 80% of micro enterprises under PMEGP are established in rural areas. In FY 2024-
25 more than 70% of the beneficiaries assisted under PMEGP are SC/ST & Women. 
Recommendation/observation 
8.  The Committee appreciates a steady increase in the budgetary allocation for KGVY, the 
Committee recommends the Ministry to continue optimizing the utilization of funds. The Ministry 
should closely monitor the progress of the schemes, especially in areas such as awareness 
building, skill enhancement, and infrastructure support, to ensure that the full potential of these 
allocations is realized for sustainable growth in the Khadi and village industries. 
(Para No.66) 
Action Taken Replies  

6 
 
The Ministry through KVIC has instituted regular review mechanisms, to closely track the fund 
utilisation, implementation and progress of KGVY schemes. 
Regular review meetings are conducted through video conferencing by the Ministry to monitor 
scheme activities, address bottlenecks and ensure timely implementation. Periodic field visits are 
also undertaken by officials of the Ministry and KVIC to assess on-ground outcomes, beneficiary 
reach, and quality of infrastructure and training interventions. 
In alignment with the Committee's emphasis on awareness building, skill enhancement and 
infrastructure support, KVIC has undertaken the following key initiatives: 
 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed between KVIC and Prasar Bharati to 
enhance brand "Khadi India" visibility through national television and radio platforms, 
aiming to broaden outreach among youth and urban consumers. 
 Multi-channel publicity campaigns have been launched through outdoor media (buses, 
metros, trains, airports) and electronic media (radio, television) to raise awareness about 
Khadi and Village Industries schemes and products. 
 Awareness programmes were organized in 17 border villages under the Vibrant Villages 
Programme (VVP) in Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and 
Ladakh to sensitize communities about KVI schemes. 
 Infrastructure of departmental training centres is being upgraded through NBCC to enhance 
the scale and quality of skill development initiatives. 
 Professional Training Associates and Local Skill Trainers have been engaged across various 
sectors such as Agro -based, Mineral -based and Service industries for specialized training 
programmes. 
 The Centre of Excellence for Khadi (CoEK) has launched a Capacity Building Training 
Program for over 370 personnel from Khadi Institutions, focusing on product development, 
production techniques and marketing skills. 
 Additionally, the Knowledge Portal for Khadi has been developed to provide a one -stop 
digital resource for skill development, design innovation, and knowledge dissemination to 
artisans and Khadi institutions. 
 The Honey processing plant at CBRTI, P une, has been refurbished and now honey 
processing plant has production capacity of 450-500 kg of honey per shift of 8 hours. 
 Central Sliver Plants (CSP), Kuttur and CSP, Chitradurga have been refurbished leading to 
an increase in production capacity by 47 % and 27% respectively. CSP, Hajipur, is currently 
under refurbishmentto ensure quality and cost-effective sliver production. 

7 
 
 Raw material supply has been strengthened through the establishment of Marino Wool Bank 
at Bikaner and Cocoon Banks at Patna and Ranchi to cater to the needs of Khadi institutions 
in Rajasthan, Bihar, and Jharkhand. 
 As part reaching out to underserved areas, A Centre for Rural Enterprise Acceleration 
through Technology (CREATE) has been established at Leh to promote local productivi ty, 
improve product quality, and strengthen livelihood opportunities for traditional artisans in 
border regions. 
 Similarly, an Eri -Silk Khadi Production -cum-Training Centre has been set up at Bomdila 
(GRL Monastery, Buddhist Culture Preservation Society) i n the Northeastern Region to 
promote traditional Khadi varieties and integrate skill development with enterprise creation. 
The Ministry remains committed to ensuring effective and outcome -oriented utilization of funds 
under KGVY through continuous monitori ng, targeted interventions, and strengthening support 
systems across the Khadi and Village Industries sector. 
Recommendation/observation 
9.  The Committee appreciates the increased allocations for the Khadi Vikas Yojana (KVY) in the 
upcoming financial year. Given the positive trajectory of the scheme, the Ministry is encouraged 
to continue this momentum and ensure full utilization of allocated funds. Furthermore, it is 
recommended that efforts be made to enhance outreach and support for Khadi artisans, 
especially in rural areas, through targeted marketing and technology adoption initiatives. 
(Para No. 67) 
Action Taken Replies  
The Ministry is committed to ensuring optimal utilization of funds to sustain and further 
strengthen the positive momentum in the Kha di sector.  In line with the Committee’s 
recommendation to enhance outreach and support for Khadi artisans, especially in rural areas, 
the following initiatives have been undertaken: 
 To strengthen brand outreach and artisan support, KVIC is leveraging strategic partnerships 
and expanded media by collaborating with Prasar Bharati for promoting “Khadi India” brand 
across national broadcasting channels, creating a strong association between Khadi and 
national identity, thereby reinforcing Khadi’s identity among both rural and urban audiences. 
This coupled with diversified marketing campaign through outdoor and electronic media 
ensures localized and mass outreach. Through these initiatives, the Ministry aims not only to  
promote awareness but also to create s teady demand pipelines, directly benefiting rural 
artisans by expanding their consumer base. 

8 
 
  KVIC, in collaboration with the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), has 
established the Centre of Excellence for Khadi (CoEK), which provides Khadi i nstitutions 
with access to contemporary designs, visual merchandising strategies, and new product 
development via a digital platform.This Knowledge Portal for Khadi has been developed as 
an e-learning and design resource hub to build capabilities of artisa ns and Khadi institutions 
for catering the urban youth. 
 E-market linkages have been strengthened through dedicated online platforms such as 
khadiindia.gov.in and integration with the Government e -Marketplace (GeM), enabling 
Khadi institutions and artisans to tap into digital sales channels. 
 Participation in major exhibitions such as the India International Trade Fair (IITF) and 
organization of Khadi -focused exhibitions at national and regional levels to provide rural 
Khadi artisans with market access opportunities. 
 
 
Recommendation/observation 
10. The Committee acknowledges the upward trend in the allocations for Gramodyog Vikas 
Yojana (GVY) in FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26. This increase is a positive sign for the promotion 
of village industries and the modernization of traditional sectors. The Committee recommends 
the Ministry focus on expanding skill development programs and modernizing infrastructure to 
ensure the competitiveness of village industries in global markets, particularly in agro -based 
and wellness industries, to maximize the impact. 
(Para No. 68) 
Action Taken Replies  
KVIC, through its departmental training centres spread across the country, is actively engaged in 
conducting specialized training programmes to create a skilled and employable workforce in the 
village industries sector. 
Professional Training Associates and Local Skill Trainers have been engaged to deliver high -
quality, market relevant training to rural beneficiaries and entrepreneurs with special emphasis 
on agro -based industries (such as food processing) and wellness industries (such as cosmetics 
and natural health products). 
Further, new skill verticals such as Air conditioner repairing, mobile repairing, sewing machine 
operator and popcorn making have also been introduced to b roaden the opportunities for rural 
entrepreneurs under GVY.  

9 
 
In order to support such initiatives, KVIC is strengthening its departmental training centers by 
upgrading infrastructure through the National Buildings Construction Corporation (NBCC) to 
accommodate modern skill requirements for enhance quality of skill development programs. 
Recommendation/observation 
11.  The Committee appreciates the effective utilization of allocated funds in SRI Fund of Funds 
in the last three years. The Committee recommends that the Ministry continue to focus on 
enhancing the fund's reach and impact by ensuring the full utilization of the proposed ₹700 crore 
allocations for FY 2025-26. The Ministry should ensure timely and efficient deployment of funds 
to maximize the scheme's benefits for the MSME sector. 
(Para No. 71) 
Action Taken Replies  
To utilize the allocated funds under SRI Fund, Monthly Expenditure Plan (MEP) based approach 
is being followed. Therefore, as per the previous trend of utilization of funds, allocated fund  
under SRI Fund of Rs. 700 crore for the current FY is expected to be  utilized timely. Further, for 
efficient deployment of fund, several outreach programme are being planned in the FY -2025-26 
and effective utilization of   funds   Investment Manager –SVL ha s been requested to facilitate 
timely demands from Daughter Funds. 
Recommendation/observation 
12.  The Committee notes that for FY 2024 -25, the Ministry has maximized the utilization of 
allocations at the RE stage in Coir Vikas Yojana. Similarly, it recomm ends that for FY 2025 -26, 
the allocated amount of Rs. 104.39 crore be utilized optimally and efficiently. If required, the 
Ministry should request an enhanced allocation at the RE stage, considering the scheme’s 
significance in supporting employment, particularly for women artisans in rural areas 
(Para No. 94) 
Action Taken Replies  
The Ministry welcomes the Committee’s recommendation and will work towards the optimal 
and efficient utilization of grants allocated for the FY 2025 -26. The Ministry may request for 
enhanced allocation, if required, at the RE stage. 
Recommendation/observation 
13. The Committee further observes that the coir industry, being traditional, holds substantial 
potential for skill development. To drive growth and expand into non -traditional areas, the 
Ministry should prioritize regular training and skill development programs, including those 

10 
 
focused on technological innovations, to enhance the capabilities of artisans and foster overall 
development in the coir sector. 
(Para No. 95) 
Action Taken Replies  
The ‘Skill Upgradation & Mahila Coir Yojana’ is one of the major sub components of the ‘Coir 
Vikas Yojana’ scheme through which the Coir Board is implementing various skill development 
activities across the country. In addition to the  regular training programmes like training in value 
added products, spinning under Mahila Coir Yojana, Certificate course &    Diploma course in 
Coir Technology, various promotional programmes like Entrepreneur Development Programme 
(EDP), Awareness programme, Seminars, Workshops, Exposure tours etc. are conducted by Coir 
Board to create awareness among the stakeholders on technological innovations, schemes and 
services available, options for credit facilities etc in Coir Industry.  
The recommendation of the Committee to focus on the expansion of activities to non traditional 
areas are acknowledged. However, in order to expand the industry into non -traditional areas the 
Coir Board are being equipped with stronger statutory support to meet emerging challenges and 
opportunities and accordingly, provisions of the Coir Industry Act are proposed to be 
amended/modified vis-à-vis the present requirements that have evolved under the influence of 
globalization, liberalization, privatization and also technological advan cements, and changing 
consumer preferences.  
Recommendation/observation 
14. The Committee observes variations in the BE and AE of the Scheme over the past two years.  
Given the underutilization of funds in FY 2024 -25 and the BE of ₹65 crore for FY 2025 -26, 
Committee recommends to focus on timely fund disbursement, enhanced outreach to MSMEs, 
and targeted capacity -building initiatives to improve fund utilization and align with actual 
absorption capacity. 
(Para No. 101) 
Action Taken Replies  
The Procurement a nd Marketing Support (PMS) Scheme plays a vital role in enhancing market

Recommendation/observation  
2.  The Committee notes that, as of December 31, 2024, out of the 5.77 crore total MSMEs, 5.69 
crore are micro, 7.3 lakhs are small, and 69,000 are medium. Despite this, the new revised 
investment and turnover limits could potentiall y undermine the purpose of MSMEs by elevating 
micro-enterprises beyond their original scope. It is recommended that the Government revise the 
definition of Micro, Small, and Medium enterprises and create a new category –nano with the 
lowest financial crite ria around ₹10 lakhs. This would ensure that businesses with a turnover 
above ₹2.5 crore do not deviate from the core purpose of MSMEs —driving employment 
generation and supporting smaller enterprises. 
(Para No. 19) 
Action Taken Replies  

29 
 
The majority of the  MSMEs fall in the category of Micro Enterprises. Through the revised 
definition of MSMEs which came into effect on 01.04.2025, an attempt has been made to 
incorporate the dynamic changes within the MSME ecosystem. Further, the Ministry has made 
special efforts to provide support to Informal Micro Enterprises (IMEs) which were about 2.7 
crore as on 31st March, 2025. These IMEs are almost 45% of the total MSMEs and do not have a 
turnover of more than Rs. 40 Lakhs. They have been made eligible for Priority Se ctor Lending 
and marketing support of the Ministry. 
Further, Special Provision for the Informal Micro Enterprises (IMEs) under Credit Guarantee 
Scheme was launched on 14.02.2024 having guarantee covers credit facilities up to Rs. 20 lakh 
with 85% coverage, with no primary security required. 
Further Recommendation/observation 
While the revised MSME definition effective from 1 st April 2025 reflects the Ministry’s 
intent to accommodate dynamic market conditions, the Committee remains concerned that 
the expanded thresholds, particularly for micro enterprises, may dilute the policy focus on 
truly small and employment -intensive units . The Ministry’s reply acknowledges that 45 
percent of MSMEs are Informal Micro Enterprises with turnover below ₹40 lakh and 
highlights recent efforts such as Priority Sector Lending eligibility and the launch of a 
dedicated Credit Guarantee Scheme with 85  percent coverage and no collateral 
requirement. However, the Committee notes that these measures, while commendable, do 
not yet constitute a formal classification or targeted scheme architecture for the smallest 
units. 
Accordingly, the Committee reiterate s its recommendation that the Ministry explore the 
creation of a distinct Nano Enterprises category within the Udyam registration framework, 
defined by investment below ₹10 lakh and turnover under ₹40 lakh. This category should 
be institutionalized in sche me design, budget planning, and performance monitoring to 
ensure focused support for micro -level entrepreneurs, particularly women, artisans, and 
rural self-employed individuals. Tailored instruments such as simplified compliance norms, 
differentiated credit scoring models, and targeted fiscal incentives should be developed to 
meet the unique needs of these units. This will ensure that genuine grassroots enterprises 
are not crowded out by relatively larger micro units nearing the ₹2.5 crore threshold and 
that the original intent of MSME policy, fostering inclusive and employment -rich 
entrepreneurship, is preserved. 
 
OVERALL BUDGETARY ALLOCATIONS & ISSUES  
Recommendation/observation 
3. The Committee notes that 96.9% of the Ministry's budget allocation is allocated to revenue 
expenditure, with only 3.1% earmarked for capital expenditure. To drive substantial growth and 
achieve encouraging outcomes, the Ministry should prioritize increasing capital expenditure, as 
this will give an impetus to infrastructure and developmental initiatives.

(Para No. 26) 
Action Taken Replies  
Most of the schemes of the Ministry are demand driven and are in Revenue Section of the Grant. 
However, funds amounting to ₹1997.21 cr. have been allocated in FY 2025 -26 for creation of 
capital assets/ infrastructure set up including machineries, equipment under various schemes.  
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
While the Committee notes the Ministry’s allocation of ₹1,997.21 crore towards capital 
assets in FY 2025–26, it remains concerned that capital expenditure continues to constitute 
only a small fraction of the overall budget. Given the critical role of infrastructure in 
enhancing productivity and competitiveness across MSME clusters, this imbalance may 
constrain long-term outcomes. Schemes such as SFURTI, MSE -CDP, and PMEGP depend 
on timely creation of Common Facility Centres, testing laboratories, and industrial 
workspaces. Persistent underutilization of capital outlay risks weakening the foundational 
support needed for MSME growth. 
The Committee therefore recommends that the Ministry conduct a scheme -wise capital 
expenditure audit to identify bottlenecks in fund deployment, project readiness, and asset 
utilization. Based on these findings, a medium -term capital investment str ategy should be 
developed with annual infrastructure targets across cluster development, skilling centres, 
and technology hubs. This strategy should be embedded within the Ministry’s outcome 
budgeting framework to ensure alignment with scheme objectives, t imely execution, and 
measurable impact. Greater emphasis on capital investment will help unlock scale 
efficiencies and strengthen the institutional ecosystem for MSMEs.

PMEGP scheme and significant disparities in production, sales, and employment across NER 
states. To boost entrepreneurship and create sustainable micro enterprises, it recommends that 
the Ministry of MSME focus on boosting entrepreneurship and micro enterprise growth in the 

38 
 
North Eastern Region (NER) by targeting underperforming states with specialized support, 
training, and mentorship. 
(Para No.115) 
Action Taken Replies  
Steps being taken to support more enterprises in North Eastern Region under the scheme include 
the following : 
(i) Beneficiaries belonging to North Eastern Region (NER) are covered under Special 
category which are provided with the Margin Money Subsidy of 35 % in rural areas 
and 25% in urban areas and 25% in urban areas as against 25% in rural areas and 15% 
in urban areas in case of General category beneficiaries. 
(ii) Own contribution of beneficiaries belonging to NER is 5% of the project cost as 
against to own contribution of 10 under General category. 
(iii) 2nd loan tranche of upto ₹ 1 crore is being provided for upgradation and expansion of 
well-performing existing PMEGP/MUDRA units with subsidy of 20% for NER and 
hilly areas as against 15% in other areas. 
(iv) There is no  ceiling on the number of projects financed under transport activities in 
NER as against the 10% ceiling on number of projects in other areas. 
(v) Industries related to Animal Husbandry like dairy, poultry, acquaculture, insects (bees, 
sericulture,etc). have been allowed under the scheme  
(vi) Awareness programme with a focus on beneficiaries from North-Eastern Region. 
(vii) As a special case, piggery, a major source of livelihood in NER, is allowed in NER 
states.  
Further Recommendation/observation 
The Committee notes th at while PMEGP provides enhanced financial incentives and 
sectoral flexibilities for beneficiaries in the North Eastern Region, several states including 
Tripura, Arunachal Pradesh, and Mizoram continue to show a declining trend in the 
number of assisted mi cro-enterprises. This indicates that existing provisions are not 
yielding uniform results across the region and that structural and operational challenges 
may be limiting uptake and impact. 
To address this, the Committee recommends that the Ministry develo p a state -specific 
implementation framework for PMEGP in the North Eastern Region. This framework 
should include quarterly performance benchmarks, localized outreach strategies, and 
capacity-building partnerships tailored to tribal communities, youth, and women 
entrepreneurs. Institutions such as the Indian Institute of Entrepreneurship in Guwahati 
and KVIC field offices should be mobilized to deliver targeted training and mentorship. 
The Committee further recommends the creation of a digital monitoring das hboard to 
track proposal quality, approval timelines, and fund disbursement across states. This will 

39 
 
enable data -driven decision -making, early identification of gaps, and timely corrective 
action to improve scheme absorption and employment outcomes in the region. 
 
Recommendation/observation  
12. The Committee observes a significant decrease in the number of women beneficiaries under 
the PMEGP scheme, with only 11,415 women entrepreneurs assisted in 2024 -25 (up to 
December), marking a nearly 69% reduction compared to the previous year. To reverse this 
decline, it recommends that the Ministry of MSME launch targeted outreach and awareness 
campaigns, particularly in areas with low participation, to encourage more women to take 
advantage of the scheme’s benefits. 
(Para No. 117) 
Action Taken Replies  
The proportion of women beneficiaries to total number of beneficiaries assisted under the 
Scheme in FY 2024 -25 is 39.23%.  The decline in number of women beneficiaries assisted (in 
absolute terms) in FY 2024 -25 is d ue to reduced budget allocation under the scheme from Rs. 
3093.87 crore in FY 2023-24 to Rs. 2202 crore in FY 2024-25.   
2. The initiatives taken under the Scheme to increase awareness and participation of women 
beneficiaries across the country are the following:   
i. Beneficiaries under Special Category including women are provided with higher 
subsidy of 25% and 35% of the project cost in urban and rural areas respectively as 
compared to 15% and 25% of the project cost for General Category beneficiaries. 
ii. Own contribution of beneficiaries belonging to Special Category including women 
is 5% of the project cost as against to own contribution of 10% under General 
category. 
iii. Awareness programmes in all the States/UTs including backward and under -
performing areas, As pirational districts, North Eastern Region with a focus on 
special category beneficiaries. 
Conduct of two -days free online Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) for 
prospective entrepreneurs. 
Further Recommendation/observation 
In addition to targeted outreach and awareness campaigns to enhance women’s 
participation under PMEGP, the Committee recommends that the Ministry of MSME, in 
collaboration with the Khadi and Village Industries Commission, develop region -specific 
promotion strategies that focus on traditional crafts, weaving, handloom, bamboo -based 

40 
 
activities, and other culturally rooted enterprises. Special emphasis should be placed on the 
North Eastern Region, where a significant number of women are engaged in heritage-based 
livelihoods that hold both economic and cultural value. 
The Committee further recommends that the Ministry identify clusters of traditional skill -
based industries and extend tailored support through skill development programmes, 
simplified access to fin ance, handholding assistance, and improved marketing linkages. To 
institutionalize this effort, the Ministry may consider introducing a dedicated sub -scheme 
or component within PMEGP to promote women -led micro -enterprises in the North 
Eastern states. This initiative should prioritise enterprises that preserve indigenous 
knowledge and contribute to sustainable community-based economic development. 
AUTONOMOUS BODIES - BUDGETING AND OTHER RELATED ISSUES 
Recommendation/observation  
13.  The Committee recommends  that the Ministry allocate additional resources to expand the 
credit support facilities, which have shown a steady rise, from ₹7,221 crore in 2022 -23 to a 
projected ₹9,450 crore in 2024-25. This growth underscores the increasing demand for financial 
assistance among MSMEs. Moreover, given the growth in the number of trainees (from 61,090 in 
2022-23 to a projected 79,200 in 2024 -25), the committee urges the Ministry to further invest in 
skill development programs, ensuring that MSMEs are equipped with the n ecessary technical 
expertise to thrive in the evolving market. 
(Para No. 132) 
Action Taken Replies  
NSIC provides short term credit support for raw material procurement by making the payment to 
suppliers under Raw Material Assistance scheme against Bank Guarantee. To meet the credit 
requirements of MSME units, NSIC has entered into Memorandum of Understa nding with 
Nationalized and Private Sector Banks. Through syndication with these banks, NSIC arranges for 
credit support (fund or non -fund-based limits) from banks. Credit support provided by NSIC to 
MSMEs during last three years are as under:

Further, NSIC Technical Services Centers are presently offering Job oriented skill development 
trainings in various disciplines as per requirement of industries. In FY2024 -25, 79295 trainees 
were trained in these technical centres. Further, NSIC with support under Assistant to Training 
Centre of the Ministry is working on a proposal to set up a Technology Centre at Peenya 
Industrial Estate, Bengalure to provide hi -tech training for skill development, material testing 
and advanced labs in a wide range of modern areas by the industries. 
Further Recommendation/observation 
While the Committee notes the steady expansion of NSIC’s credit support from ₹7,221 
crore in FY 2022–23 to ₹8,527 crore in FY 2024 –25, and the scale of skill training reaching 
nearly 79,295 trainees, it remains concerned about the absence of a structured mechanism 
to evaluate the effectiveness of credit deployment and the employment outcomes of skilling 
initiatives. To address this, the Committee recommends that the Ministry establish a credit 
utilization and impact tracking framework under NSIC’s syndication model. This 
framework should capture key indicators such as l oan conversion rates, repayment 
performance, sector -wise credit distribution, and the extent to which credit support 
contributes to enterprise growth and formalization. 
The Committee further recommends that the Ministry expedite the establishment of the 
proposed Technology Centre at Peenya Industrial Estate and develop a roadmap to 
replicate similar advanced training hubs in other high -density industrial clusters. These 
centres should be designed to deliver industry -aligned curricula, incorporate digital an d 
sustainable technologies, and offer placement -linked skilling modules. Integration with 
local MSME networks and sector -specific associations will help ensure that training is 
demand-driven and leads to measurable improvements in productivity, innovation,  and 
employment generation. 
Recommendation/observation  
14. The Committee observes a decline in new member registrations under the Single Point 
Registration Scheme (SPRS), despite an overall increase in units served. To address this, it 
recommends that the  Ministry intensify efforts to encourage MSMEs, particularly in high -
potential sectors, to register under the SPRS. Additionally, given the projected rise in agency 
sales to ₹4,500 crore in 2024 -25, the Ministry may enhance market access for MSME products,  
ensuring a robust and expanding customer base. 
(Para No.133) 
 
Action Taken Replies  
NSIC operates Single Point Registration Scheme (SPRS) for Government purchase to build the 
capacities of MSE for participation in Government tenders and contribute in Government Public 
Procurement processes. The units registered under Single Point Registration Scheme of NSIC are 
eligible to get the benefits under Public Procurement Policy for Micro & Small Enterprises 

42 
 
(MSE) Order, 2012. 14140 units were served under SPRS during FY 2024 -25. The decline in the 
new member registration under SPRS Scheme is due to the non -recognition of the SPRS 
Certificate at GEM Portal. Rigorously follow -up is being made by NSIC with GEM in this 
regard. 
Further Recommendation/observation     
 
While the Committee acknowledges NSIC’s efforts to expand SPRS coverage and the 
servicing of 14,140 units in FY 2024 –25, it remains concerned that the non -recognition of 
SPRS certificates on the Government e -Marketplace portal is limiting new registrations 
and weakening the operational link between registration and procurement benefit s. This 
disconnect risks discouraging MSMEs from formalizing and participating in public 
procurement, thereby undermining the objectives of the Public Procurement Policy for 
Micro and Small Enterprises. 
To address this, the Committee recommends that the Mi nistry, in coordination with NSIC 
and the Ministry of Commerce, establish a technical integration protocol to enable 
seamless recognition of SPRS credentials on the GeM portal. This should include 
automated verification, real -time data exchange, and alignm ent of eligibility criteria. The 
Committee further recommends launching a joint outreach and onboarding campaign 
targeting MSMEs in high -growth sectors such as manufacturing, clean energy, and digital 
services. This campaign should clarify the benefits of SPRS registration, simplify the 
application process, and promote participation in government tenders. These measures will 
help restore trust in the scheme and ensure that procurement -linked incentives are 
effectively delivered to eligible enterprises.
